title: Sex-Specific Myostatin-Grey Matter Volume Associations in Ageing Adults: Implications for the Muscle-Brain Axis.
journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for cognitive decline, suggesting bidirectional muscle-brain crosstalk mediated by myokines. Myostatin, a negative regulator of muscle growth, may influence brain health through systemic signalling, yet human neuroimaging evidence remains lacking. Moreover, men and women exhibit distinct patterns of muscle ageing and cognitive decline, but sex-specific effects of myostatin on brain structure have not been investigated. This study examined associations between serum myostatin and regional brain grey matter volume (GMV) in ageing adults, with emphasis on sexual dimorphism. We analysed 482 community-dwelling participants (235 males, 247 females; mean age 67.2 ± 8.5 years, range of 50-88) from the I-Lan Longitudinal Aging Study. Serum myostatin levels, muscle mass and grip strength were assessed. High-resolution brain MRI was processed using voxel-based morphometry to examine associations between myostatin and regional GMV. Sex-stratified analyses were performed, adjusting for age, muscle metrics and total intracranial volume, with multiple comparison correction (cluster-level FWE p 0.95). Notably, height-adjusted muscle mass correlated with grip strength in men (r = 0.204, p = 0.002) but not women (r = 0.075, p = 0.240). Neuroimaging revealed complete sexual dimorphism with zero overlapping brain regions. In men, higher myostatin associated with larger GMV in left postcentral gyrus but smaller GMV in right cerebellum VIIIb. In women, higher myostatin associated exclusively with smaller GMV across three regions: left inferior temporal gyrus, right frontal pole and right postcentral gyrus. Sensitivity analyses using the ratio of myostatin to relative appendicular skeletal muscle mass (RASM) reproduced the primary associations and revealed additional negative associations in the left cerebellum Crus I in men and in the left temporal pole and left middle temporal gyrus in women. Myostatin demonstrated pronounced sex-specific associations with brain structure, with complete sexual dimorphism. Women exhibited exclusively negative myostatin-GMV relationships across cognitive and sensorimotor regions, whereas men showed mixed patterns. These findings provide the first human neuroimaging evidence for sexual dimorphism in the muscle-brain axis. Given that sarcopenia confers two-to threefold greater cognitive impairment risk in women, elevated myostatin may represent a sex-specific biomarker linking muscle wasting to neurodegeneration.

title: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Intramuscular Olanzapine Versus Haloperidol for Acute Agitation in Hospitalized Adult Women With Bipolar I Disorder.
abstract: To compare intramuscular (IM) olanzapine and haloperidol for acute agitation in hospitalized women with bipolar I disorder during a manic episode, with or without mixed features. In this single-center, double-blind, active-controlled randomized trial, 40 female inpatients were assigned to IM olanzapine 10 mg (n = 20) or haloperidol 5 mg (n = 20). The primary outcome was the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS); secondary outcomes were the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale-Excited Component (PANSS-EC) and Modified Simpson-Angus Scale (MSAS), assessed at 15 min, 1 h, and 24 h. No numerical pretreatment outcome scores were available. All participants completed follow-up. RASS scores changed over time (p = 0.030), but the group-by-time interaction (p = 0.777) and overall group effect (p = 0.880) were not significant. PANSS-EC showed an overall group effect (p = 0.043), with lower mean scores in the olanzapine group; however, the interaction (p = 0.662) and individual time-point comparisons were not significant. MSAS scores were low in the olanzapine group and zero in the haloperidol group. One participant receiving haloperidol experienced excessive sedation; no other adverse events were recorded. RASS trajectories did not differ significantly between groups. Lower overall PANSS-EC scores with olanzapine are exploratory and do not establish treatment superiority. The small sample and absence of pretreatment measurements limit interpretation; these findings require confirmation in larger trials. IRCT20230131057294N1.

title: Lipid regulation of autophagy flux and neurodegeneration.
abstract: Autophagy is a lysosomal degradation pathway crucial for the maintenance of proteostasis, organelle quality control, and stress adaptation. Autophagosomes form from finger-like structures emanating from the recycling endosome, called phagophores, which capture cytoplasmic cargo before closing like a fist. These closed structures are then released from the recycling endosome by dynamin 2 to form autophagosomes that ultimately fuse with lysosomes, where their contents are degraded. In the central nervous system, autophagy protects against the cytoplasmic accumulation of toxic, aggregate-prone proteins and damaged organelles, common features of neurodegenerative diseases such as Huntington's and Alzheimer's disease. Lipids have emerged as crucial mediators of autophagosome biogenesis and have multifaceted effects on autophagic flux. At the edges of the phagophore, coordinated lipid transfer from donor membranes and scramblase activity support appropriate lipid bilayer formation and membrane expansion. In addition, the highly curved, loosely packed lipids at the phagophore edges act as a platform for binding of key autophagy effectors via their amphipathic domains and promote autophagosome maturation. The role of lipids extends beyond structural support in autophagosome formation and includes modulation of upstream signalling pathways, establishment of autophagic membrane identity, and lysosomal maintenance. Autophagy itself contributes to the maintenance of lipid homeostasis via the selective lipid droplet degradation pathway termed lipophagy. Importantly, alterations in lipid composition and metabolism have been demonstrated to impair autophagic flux and contribute to the development of several sporadic and inherited neurological disorders.

title: Acute Reperfusion Therapies for Medium and Distal Vessel Occlusions.
abstract: Medium and distal vessel occlusions (MDVO) account for a substantial proportion of acute ischemic strokes (AIS) and carry a considerable burden of long-term disability. The optimal acute reperfusion strategy for these occlusions remains uncertain. We aimed to synthesize the current evidence on intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), endovascular treatment (EVT), and intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) for MDVO. We conducted a narrative review of randomized-controlled clinical trials (RCTs), observational studies, and meta-analyses, complemented by updated meta-analyses of randomized data where feasible. The definition of MDVO remains inconsistent complicating the interpretation and pooling of evidence. IVT achieves recanalization in a minority of distal occlusions, yet retains benefit, including in extended time windows. In our updated meta-analysis of five RCTs, EVT did not improve functional outcomes compared with best medical treatment while increasing symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Reperfusion benefit across modalities appears to vary according to stroke severity, occlusion location, timing, and tissue viability. IAT, which delivers thrombolytics directly to the occlusion while minimizing mechanical manipulation of fragile distal vessels, is under investigation as a targeted alternative, with numerous dedicated RCTs ongoing but none yet published. No single reperfusion strategy serves this heterogeneous population uniformly. IVT remains the reperfusion therapy with established benefit for most patients with MDVO, whereas EVT has not improved outcomes in unselected MDVO and IAT remains investigational. Pending further evidence, management beyond IVT should remain cautious rather than routine.

title: Are two readings as good as three for monthly linear accelerator output quality assurance?
journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
abstract: During monthly linear accelerator (linac) output quality assurance (QA), it is common practice to acquire three consecutive ionization chamber readings per beam energy and average them. Whether two readings carry the same QA decisions in practice has not been directly quantified against historical output data. This study evaluates whether reducing the number of readings per monthly output measurement from three to two preserves QA decision accuracy against the TG-142 ± 2% action threshold. Within-session variation was additionally evaluated against the ± 0.5% between-reading criterion of TG-198. A retrospective analysis was performed on three years of monthly output QA data from four linear accelerators at a single institution, across eight beam energies (6, 9, 12, and 16 MeV electrons; 6, 6 FFF, 10, and 15 MV photons), with each check comprising three consecutive readings per energy. The analysis combined four components: (i) a paired-difference comparison of per-session means from two-reading versus three-reading protocols, summarized with mean differences, percent differences, and Cohen's d; (ii) an evaluation of within-session reading variation against the TG-198 criterion; (iii) a scenario analysis of false-positive and false-negative classifications against the TG-142 action threshold, with the three-reading decision taken as ground truth; and (iv) generalized linear mixed-effects modeling of individual readings, with random intercepts for machine and measurement session, to test for systematic reading-order shifts. Across all eight energies, the absolute mean difference between two- and three-reading protocols was at most 0.006 nC, corresponding to less than 0.04% of the corrected output. The two protocols produced concordant pass/fail decisions in 961 of 963 recorded sessions (99.1-100% per energy). The two-reading protocol produced no false negatives: the two sessions above the action threshold were detected by both protocols, and the only disagreements were two isolated false alarms (one at 6 MeV, one at 6 MV). Within-session reading variation satisfied the TG-198 ± 0.5% criterion in 91.9-100% of sessions per energy, and restricting attention to the first two readings never increased the fraction of sessions exceeding that criterion. Mixed-effects modeling identified a small but statistically detectable reading-order shift: relative to the first reading, the second and third photon readings were lower by approximately 0.05% and 0.12%, and the corresponding electron shifts were near 0.05%. In all cases the absolute magnitude of these shifts was below 0.18%, well within the ± 0.5% between-reading variation limit recommended by TG-198. For the eight beam energies studied, monthly output QA decisions based on two readings were consistent with those based on three readings, with no false negatives and a reading-order effect well within the TG-198 ± 0.5% limit. Low-energy electron beams (non-normal repeatability, the largest single outlier) and 10 MV (most frequent exceedance of the 0.5% criterion) warrant closer attention. These results indicate that two-reading protocols can maintain QA decision accuracy while reducing measurement time.

title: Peri-irradiation GABA-B receptor modulation and central precocious puberty after cranial irradiation: A neuroendocrine perspective.
abstract: Cranial irradiation can disrupt hypothalamic-pituitary function and is associated with early or central precocious puberty (CPP), particularly in girls treated at a young age. A small but influential rodent literature suggests that low-dose cranial irradiation can accelerate pubertal development, reduce stimulated hypothalamic gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) release, and increase gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) expression. These observations justify asking whether a brief pharmacological change in neuronal state around irradiation could modify evolving hypothalamic injury and preserve age-appropriate pubertal timing, while recognizing that radiation may be only one component of the causal pathway. This Perspective develops that question around peri-irradiation GABA-B receptor modulation, using baclofen as a tractable mechanistic probe rather than as a proposed clinical treatment. GABA-B activation can reduce transmitter release and neuronal firing, but its reproductive effects depend on receptor location, developmental stage, sex-steroid milieu, and species. It may inhibit GnRH secretion directly, reduce GABA release through presynaptic autoreceptors, or alter upstream kisspeptin and monoaminergic networks. Thus, the biologically defensible hypothesis is not that baclofen simply restores inhibitory GABA tone. Rather, transient GABA-B modulation might alter secondary oxidative, mitochondrial, inflammatory, or cell-death pathways during irradiation and thereby preserve network function over time. This neuroprotective step is the least-supported part of the proposed causal chain and remains unproven in the prepubertal irradiated hypothalamus. Primary ionization and the initial radiation-induced DNA damage would remain unaffected. We separate established observations from inference, identify competing explanations, and propose a staged experimental program using clinically informed fractionated irradiation and tumor-bearing models, with pharmacological-only controls, cell-resolved acute endpoints, longitudinal LH dynamics as a physiological proxy for GnRH pulse-generator function, and pubertal phenotyping. The hypothesis should advance only if reduced secondary injury can be dissociated from acute endocrine suppression and from nonspecific sedation, hypothermia, or nutritional effects. The central novelty is the proposed peri-irradiation GABA-B perturbation as a test of state-dependent hypothalamic radioprotection, not the established association between cranial irradiation, altered GABA/GnRH signaling, and early puberty. This framework therefore reframes a speculative prophylactic idea as a falsifiable neuroendocrine research agenda.

title: Proximity-Induced Targeted Degradation of Microtubule-Associated Protein Tau Pre-mRNA Using Small Bifunctional Molecules.
abstract: Dysregulation of RNA processing caused by single-nucleotide mutations can profoundly alter cellular homeostasis and drive disease. A prominent example is the aberrant alternative splicing of the microtubule-associated protein tau (MAPT) gene, which leads to imbalances in 3R and 4R tau isoforms and is associated with multiple tauopathies. In particular, mutations such as the disinhibition-dementia-parkinsonism-amyotrophy complex (DDPAC) variant promote exon 10 inclusion, increasing the 4R/3R ratio and contributing to tau aggregation and neurodegeneration. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) can reduce MAPT mRNA levels, while small molecules have been developed to modulate MAPT pre-mRNA splicing by targeting regulatory RNA structures. Here, we investigated an alternative approach based on Proximity-Induced Nucleic Acid Degradation (PINAD), in which an RNA-binding ligand is conjugated to an RNA-cleaving warhead. We designed and synthesized a library of 24 bifunctional small molecules derived from a previously reported MAPT pre-mRNA SRE-binding ligand. Screening in SH-SY5Y cells identified PINAD-23, which reduced MAPT mRNA levels in a dose-dependent manner and decreased the expression of both 3R and 4R tau isoforms. Biochemical studies using a model MAPT RNA showed that PINAD-23 binds the target RNA and promotes RNA cleavage. Defined cleavage products detected under metal-free conditions supported a contribution from a base-mediated pathway, while Cu(II) binding by the diimidazole warhead and Cu(II)-dependent RNA cleavage supported the involvement of a copper-dependent pathway. These findings provide a proof of concept for converting a previously characterized MAPT RNA-binding ligand into a bifunctional small molecule capable of inducing target RNA cleavage and reducing downstream tau expression.

title: Shedding Light on Autophagy: Autophagy-Light Signalling Crosstalk Shaping Growth and Metabolism.
abstract: Light is both an energy source and a regulatory signal that shapes plant development, metabolism and environmental acclimation. Autophagy, a conserved degradation and recycling pathway, maintains cellular homoeostasis by reallocating resources and removing damaged components. Although these processes have often been studied separately, emerging evidence reveals that light signalling and autophagy are mechanistically intertwined. In this review, we examine how spectral cues, circadian timing, photodamage and metabolic status converge on autophagy to balance growth with cellular recycling. We highlight transcriptional and epigenetic control of ATG genes, metabolic regulation via the TOR-SnRK1 axis, selective autophagic turnover of light-signalling regulators and organelle quality-control pathways that remove damaged chloroplasts, peroxisomes and mitochondria. We further discuss how this interface contributes to darkness-associated carbon remobilisation, senescence-linked nitrogen recycling, lipophagy and possible connection with specialised metabolism. Finally, we highlight conceptual and technical gaps and propose experimental strategies, including spectral manipulation, autophagy reporters, phosphoproteomics and optogenetic approaches, to dissect the light-autophagy interface. By consolidating these insights, we provide a blueprint for testing how interactions between light signalling and autophagy affect plant stress resilience and metabolic output, and whether they contribute to developmental plasticity.

title: Reply to: "Time to nephrectomy in pT1b-2 renal cancer and the decision made at diagnosis".
Global Trends and Translational Hotspots in Phantom Limb Pain Research: A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: Phantom limb pain (PLP) research spans neuroscience, rehabilitation, and peripheral nerve interventions, yet this literature has rarely been examined as a single bibliometric corpus. We mapped its contributors, cited knowledge base, and temporal patterns to identify areas of research attention and clarify how the field has developed. English-language articles and reviews were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on January 18, 2026 using two complementary topic-search blocks. VOSviewer and CiteSpace were used to analyze co-authorship, co-citation, author-keyword co-occurrence, mean publication years, and bursts. Burst analyses covered 1990-2025. An exploratory metadata classification examined selected peripheral nerve intervention subtopics. The corpus comprised 556 publications, including one dated 2026. Annual output ranged from 27 to 39 publications during 2018-2025 and peaked in 2022. The United States led publication output (243 publications) and betweenness centrality, whereas Germany had the highest country co-authorship total link strength. Pain and Brain were the most frequently co-cited journals. Targeted muscle reinnervation had the strongest keyword burst during 2020-2025. Selected peripheral nerve intervention subtopics appeared in 78 publications (14.0%); their representation was higher in 2020-2025 than in 2014-2019 (33.5% vs. 5.3%). The selected PLP literature combined a substantial pain and neuroscience knowledge base with more recent attention to rehabilitation technologies and peripheral nerve interventions. These patterns highlight areas of research attention but do not establish comparative treatment effectiveness. Future studies should distinguish pain phenotypes and intervention timing and assess sustained patient-centered outcomes.

title: Paraclinical Fulfillment of the 2017 and 2024 McDonald Criteria in MS-Mimicking Conditions: A Multicentre Real-World Study.
abstract: The 2024 revision of the McDonald criteria expands the role of paraclinical evidence to expedite multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis while aiming to preserve diagnostic accuracy. How these changes impact diagnostic specificity in MS-mimicking conditions remains uncertain. We retrospectively identified patients from eight Italian centers with a confirmed non-MS diagnosis who presented with a first demyelinating-like event. All underwent baseline CSF analysis and brain and spinal cord MRI within four months of onset, with subsequent follow-up imaging. Paraclinical diagnostic components of the 2017 and 2024 McDonald criteria were applied, excluding the "no better explanation" clause, and fulfillment rates were compared using McNemar's test. Among 119 patients (MOGAD, n = 74; AQP4 + NMOSD, n = 31; seronegative-NMOSD, n = 3; other, n = 11), 58 (48.7%) fulfilled paraclinical diagnostic requirements under the 2024 framework, compared with 44 (37.0%) under the 2017 framework (p = 0.0005). This increase was largely attributable to optic nerve involvement, accounting for 71% of additional cases, and was consistent across major diagnostic subgroups. Expanded paraclinical definitions in the 2024 McDonald criteria increase the proportion of MS-mimics fulfilling diagnostic requirements, predominantly through optic nerve involvement. These findings underscore the importance of careful differential diagnosis and highlight that, under the 2024 criteria, the 'no better explanation' principle is even more critical to prevent misdiagnosis.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content in Manuscripts Submitted to Annals of Neurology.
abstract: Since the large language model (LLM) program Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT) was introduced in November 2022, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) expanded rapidly in published writing. This has been quantified in many fields, but not in medical journals that focus on neurology and neuroscience. We sought to characterize the use of LLM in articles submitted before and after ChatGPT became available to the general public, in a neurology journal, Annals of Neurology, that covers all neurology subspecialties. The study evaluated manuscripts submitted on movement disorders, dementia, and vascular neurology before and after ChatGPT became available. AI content was measured with LLM-detection platforms Pangram, Originality.ai and GPTZero. Substantial AI was defined as ≥20% of content, or >50% likelihood of AI use. Manuscript type, country of author, country, Human Development Index (HDI), AI disclosure, and publication decision were compared with AI detected. Of 300 papers submitted after the introduction of ChatGPT, AI was detected by Pangram in 74 (25%) and this was substantial (≥20% of content) in 32 (11%). Substantial AI was more common in brief communications than full research articles (31% vs 10%, p = 0.006) and in vascular neurology articles (17%, vascular; 8%, dementia; and 5%, movement disorders; p = 0.012). Most manuscripts analyzed were submitted by authors from China (37%) and the United States (19%) and each had 11% substantial AI use. Authors from countries with lower levels of development were more likely to use AI (median HDI 0.797, AI ≥20% vs median HDI 0.925, AI <20%, p = 0.033). No AI was found in 60 papers submitted from July 3 to September 14, 2022 (pre-ChatGPT) by any of the AI-detection platforms. Of 300 post-ChatGPT manuscripts, 24 (8%) were accepted. None with substantial AI use were accepted (p = 0.090; odds ratio [OR] = 0.000, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.000-1.068). The authors of 5 (2%) of these papers disclosed AI use, including 1 (3%) of the papers with substantial AI detected. The study found AI was used in writing one quarter of papers submitted to Annals of Neurology after ChatGPT was introduced, with substantial AI content in 11%. No papers with AI ≥20% of content were accepted for publication. AI-generated text was more frequent in brief communications and vascular neurology articles. Authors in countries with lower levels of development were significantly more likely to use AI. The results suggest no advantage from AI in publication success, but point to a need for greater transparency by authors about AI use. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: The Piezo1 Paradox in Aging and Age-Related Disease: Bidirectional Mechanosensory Dysfunction and Therapeutic Implications.
abstract: Aging is accompanied by profound changes in the mechanical properties of tissues, driving cellular dysfunction, and age-related diseases. Central to this process is Piezo1, a key mechanosensitive ion channel that converts physical stimuli into intracellular Ca2+ signals. This review synthesizes current evidence illustrating the dual, context-dependent role of Piezo1 in aging-termed the "Piezo1 Paradox." In certain tissues such as bone and bone marrow stromal cells, aging is associated with a loss of Piezo1 function, impairing mechanotransduction, and tissue maintenance. Conversely, in vascular, fibrotic, and some metabolic tissues, aging leads to Piezo1 overactivation, promoting inflammation, fibrosis, and cellular senescence. We explore how these divergent changes contribute to prevalent age-related disorders including osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and metabolic dysfunction. Furthermore, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies that aim to restore Piezo1 signaling within a tissue-specific "Goldilocks zone," highlighting pharmacological modulators, biophysical interventions, and targeted delivery systems. By framing Piezo1 as a tunable mechanosensory node, this review underscores its potential as a therapeutic target for promoting healthy aging and mitigating age-related pathologies.

title: Spinal Cord Injury-Induced HDL Remodeling Contributes to Accelerated Atherosclerosis.
abstract: Individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) develop accelerated atherosclerosis that is incompletely explained by traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Although elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is strongly associated with atherosclerosis in the general population, lipoprotein profiles after SCI are characterized by reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) without LDL-C elevation, suggesting altered HDL biology. In this study, we examined HDL composition and function in humans and animals with SCI. In humans, HDL-C was reduced in both the subacute (1-6 months) and chronic (>1 year) phases after SCI. Subacute plasma proteomics revealed remodeling of HDL protein networks, including loss of structural apolipoproteins and enrichment of complement and innate immune proteins. Functionally, HDL from SCI mice promoted proinflammatory macrophage gene expression relative to sham HDL. Finally, deletion of apolipoprotein A-I, the principal structural apolipoprotein of HDL, attenuated atherosclerosis following SCI in vivo. Together, these findings identify proinflammatory HDL remodeling as a mechanism contributing to accelerated atherosclerosis after SCI.

title: Remote heating implants enable controlled local low-intensity hyperthermia to synergize with heat-sensitive liposomal drug delivery systems in hepatocellular carcinoma.
journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
abstract: Heat-sensitive liposomal drug delivery systems (HSLDDS) have faced challenges in translation largely due to inadequate delivery of hyperthermia in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study evaluates the feasibility of using remote heating implants (RHIs) as a controlled method to deliver hyperthermia ideally suited to improve the performance of HSLDDS. Transcriptomic profiling of HCC cell line SNU423 was performed after exposure to a range of hyperthermic temperatures to identify the heating window that minimized chemotherapy resistance gene expression. RHIs were built and their heating profiles assessed through numerical modeling and performance validated through a phantom model. RHIs were implanted into an in vivo subcutaneous mouse HCC model, and heat-sensitive liposomes loaded with the fluorescent dye DiI (DiI liposomes) were injected intratumorally. Heating was applied using the RHIs to facilitate dye release. Bulk RNA sequencing revealed significant upregulation of chemotherapy resistance markers including HSP90, HSP27, HSP70, ABCB1, ABCC2, and ABCC5 at 47 °C (high-intensity hyperthermia) compared with 42 °C (low-intensity hyperthermia). RHIs maintained a stable temperature profile of 42.0 ± 0.5 °C at 1 mm and 40.3 ± 0.2 °C at 5 mm in phantoms and 42.0 ± 0.4 °C in vivo. DiI fluorescence intensity was significantly higher with 1-h heating (16.4 ± 2.3) compared with unheated controls (2.1 ± 0.9, p < 0.05). RHIs are a novel heating platform that can be used to maintain a long-term low-intensity hyperthermic environment. This heating can synergize with HSLDDS to enhance drug release against HCC while potentially avoiding chemotherapy resistance pathways induced by high-intensity hyperthermia.

title: Barriers to successful ECMO clinical research: A ClinicalTrials.gov analysis of trial termination.
journal: The International journal of artificial organs
abstract: The rate, timing, reasons, and correlates of premature study termination have not been described for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Cross-sectional analysis of ECMO-focused studies on ClinicalTrials.gov (retrieved 22 May 2026) with blinded re-screening and adjudication. Reasons for termination were coded independently by two reviewers. Associations were tested with Fisher's exact, Firth logistic, and cause-specific Cox models, with completion as a competing event. Of 450 studies, 36 (8.0%, 95% CI 5.8%-10.9%) had been terminated or withdrawn, with cumulative incidences of 8.9% at 3 years and 11.7% at five. Sponsor or organizational decisions (36.1%) and recruitment failure (33.3%) led the reasons, and none was stopped for safety. After adjustment, no design characteristic was independently associated with termination. The unadjusted FDA excess was explained by United States location (adjusted OR 9.82, 95% CI 4.17-23.49). Recruitment status was unknown for 27.4% of non-United States versus 5.4% of United States studies. About one in 12 registered ECMO studies had been terminated or withdrawn, rising to one in 8 by 5 years. Discontinuation was attributed to organizational and recruitment factors rather than to safety, and the United States excess likely reflects differences in registry reporting practice.

title: Breaking barriers: advanced targeted drug delivery strategies for sensorineural hearing loss.
abstract: Sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) is the most prevalent form of hearing impairment worldwide. However, drug delivery to the inner ear is severely hindered by the enclosed bony labyrinth and the highly selective blood-labyrinth barrier (BLB), resulting in suboptimal therapeutic outcomes and confining pharmacological management largely to symptomatic rather than etiological intervention. This review systematically dissects the multifaceted barriers to inner ear drug delivery and focuses on three core strategic pillars: (i) optimization of administration routes to balance invasiveness with cochlear bioavailability; (ii) rational selection of viral and non‑viral vectors guided by the unique pharmacokinetic properties of inner ear fluids; and (iii) functional modification of delivery systems with cell‑specific ligands to achieve precision targeting.Particular emphasis is placed on breakthrough advances such as LRP1‑mediated noninvasive trans-barrier delivery and prestin‑targeting peptide‑directed selective outer hair cell engagement. By integrating insights from drug delivery science, gene therapy, and targeted delivery research, this review proposes a conceptual framework to facilitate the clinical translation of precision medicine for SNHL. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from 189 peer-reviewed articles identified through a systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase databases (published between 1984 and 2026, focusing on advanced strategies to overcome the blood-labyrinth barrier (BLB).

title: Gamified Digital Health Interventions for Physical Activity and Sedentary Behavior Changes in Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience disproportionately higher rates of preventable chronic diseases. Gamified digital health interventions (DHIs) targeting physical activity (PA) and sedentary behavior (SB) represent a promising approach to help reduce these risks. This scoping review explored and characterized gamified DHIs developed to support PA and SB behavior change among individuals with ASD. In accordance with JBI Scoping Review Methodology and PRISMA Extension for Scoping Review guidelines, six databases were searched, and 808 records were identified, with an additional five studies found through hand-searching. Following eligibility screening, 13 studies were included in this review. Relevant data from included studies were extracted, charted, and narratively described. This review examined intervention characteristics, including target populations (i.e., adults and youth), implementation settings (e.g., school, home), intervention modalities (e.g., gaming systems, mobile apps), gamification elements (e.g., avatars, points, stories/themes), and outcome measures for PA and SB (e.g., self-report and objective). Seven studies specifically compared the effectiveness of DHIs to a control condition. Findings were mixed, with five studies reporting significant improvements in PA and/or SB through gamified DHIs when compared with a control condition, whereas two studies showed limited or nonsignificant effects. This scoping review underscores the potential of gamified DHIs to support PA- and SB-related behavior change in individuals with ASD by enhancing enjoyment and motivation. Nevertheless, the mixed evidence on effectiveness highlights the need for further research to identify the most impactful strategies for improving health behaviors in this population.

title: Photoacoustic Brain Imaging in Mice.
abstract: Photoacoustic brain imaging (PABI) has emerged as a promising modality that partially overcomes the trade-off between spatial resolution and penetration depth in conventional neuroimaging. By integrating optical absorption contrast with ultrasonic detection, PABI enables high-resolution visualization of cerebral vasculature and supports multi-parametric analysis of vascular morphological features, as well as quantitative assessment of functional oxygenation parameters such as cerebral oxygen saturation (sO2). In addition, PABI combined with exogenous tracers provides opportunities to evaluate blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and track brain lymphatic drainage dynamics. Here, we present a standardized and reproducible workflow for PABI, covering system calibration, animal preparation, experimental procedures, image acquisition, and quantitative analysis. This protocol consists of a basic imaging procedure and several optional modules, providing a practical methodological tool for applying PABI to neuroscience research.

title: Influence of regional white matter lesion volume differences related to cardiorespiratory fitness on cognition in healthy older adults.
abstract: Greater cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) has been associated with reduced global burden of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) lesions, a neuroimaging marker of small vessel cerebrovascular disease, and lower risk of age-related cognitive impairment and dementia. However, little is known about how CRF relates to regional patterns of WMH volume and the associated impact on cognitive aging. In a cohort of 166 community-dwelling, healthy older adults (mean age = 70.49 ± 9.96 years, 48.8% women), we investigated the association of CRF with regionally distributed WMH burden using multivariate regional network analysis of hemispheric lobar WMH volumes. We additionally evaluated the moderating role of CRF-related regional WMH volumetric differences for cognition. Higher CRF, distinct from self-reported habitual physical activity, was associated with a distributed covariance pattern of WMH volume reductions in bilateral frontal and right parietal lobes, with relative increases in bilateral occipital lobes. Greater CRF-WMH pattern expression was associated with younger age and male sex. Additionally, there was a significant age-by-CRF-WMH network pattern interaction for memory, but not for information processing speed and executive functioning, such that the higher the pattern expression, the weaker the inverse association between age and memory performance. Our findings suggest that having greater CRF may help to maintain cerebrovascular health in older adults as reflected in its association with reduced WMH burden in regions particularly vulnerable to brain aging and associated memory dysfunction. Multivariate CRF-WMH pattern expression may provide a marker of cerebrovascular health that may help to identify those at increased risk for age-related cognitive impairment.

title: Visualizing the inferior alveolar nerve in magnetic resonance images: a systematic review of different sequences.
abstract: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the visualization and delineation performance of different magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences for inferior alveolar nerve (IAN), focusing on detectability, image quality, and observer agreement. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library for studies published until 1 March 2025. Eligible studies assessed MRI sequences for IAN visualization in adults. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Twenty-five studies (1998-2024) were included, with sample sizes ranging from 5 to 85 participants. Most of these studies had a low risk of bias. MRI achieved high visualization performance of the IAN, often exceeding 90%. Advanced sequences such as DESS, STIR, SPACE STIR, CISS, and fat-suppressed protocols provided promising results in visualizing continuity and tissue contrast compared to conventional imaging and CBCT within individual studies. Diffusion-based imaging enabled tractography with reproducibility up to ICC 0.97. Novel approaches including PETRA UTE, zero-TE MRI, and MR orthopantomograms allowed radiographic-like bone visualization without radiation. VIBE sequence performed well but was more susceptible to artifacts, while SPACE STIR required longer acquisition times. In conclusion, MRI sequences, particularly DESS, STIR, and other optimized high-resolution protocols, demonstrate promising performance for IAN visualization and delineation. However, the heterogeneity of outcome measures and the limited availability of independent reference standards preclude definitive conclusions regarding diagnostic accuracy. Further studies using appropriate reference standards and clinically representative populations are needed to establish the diagnostic value of MRI for preoperative assessment.

title: Higher Serum Dopamine is Associated with Higher CSF Aβ42/40, Lower Amyloid-PET Burden, and Better Cognitive Function Across the Alzheimer's Disease Spectrum.
abstract: Dopaminergic dysfunction has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its relationship with amyloid pathology and cognitive impairment remains insufficiently understood. This study examined whether serum dopamine is associated with CSF amyloid-β 42/40 (Aβ42/40), amyloid-PET burden, and cognitive function across the clinical diagnostic groups in ADNI, and whether amyloid biomarkers show cross-sectional statistical indirect effects in the dopamine-cognition relationship. Cross-sectional data were obtained from ADNI, including 428 participants: cognitively normal (CN; n = 138), individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI; n = 206), and patients with AD dementia (n = 84). All analyses were performed with FDR correction to account for multiple comparisons. The results showed that serum dopamine decreased progressively from CN to MCI and AD dementia, whereas CSF Aβ42/40 decreased and amyloid-PET burden increased across diagnostic stages, accompanied by progressive worsening of cognitive function. In the pooled cohort and within MCI, higher serum dopamine was significantly associated with a more favorable amyloid profile, reflected by higher CSF Aβ42/40 and lower amyloid-PET burden, as well as better cognitive function. Cross-sectional indirect-effect analyses involving CSF Aβ42/40 met the reported FDR threshold in the pooled cohort and in MCI participants. In contrast, PET indirect effects did not remain significant after FDR correction. Overall, higher serum dopamine was linked to a more favorable amyloid profile and better cognitive function in the pooled cohort and within MCI. However, future longitudinal and mechanistic studies are needed to validate these findings, clarify causality, and characterize the peripheral dopamine-amyloid-cognition association. Serum dopamine is not a direct measure of central neurotransmission, and these subgroup results do not establish different effects between diagnoses.

title: Late cortical dynamics mediate numerosity illusions induced by symmetry.
abstract: Numerosity perception enables us to quickly estimate the number of objects in a visual scene, a fundamental skill supporting efficient interaction with the environment. In this study, we tracked how the human brain transforms physical inputs into numerical percepts. Using EEG, we characterized the temporal dynamics of how numerosity-related signals are integrated with spatial configuration cues that shape perception. We leveraged on a visual illusion in which dot arrays appear less numerous when arranged symmetrically rather than randomly. Participants viewed dot arrays of varying physical or perceived numerosity, illusorily altered by the dots' spatial arrangement. Both univariate and multivariate analyses revealed that physical numerosity was decodable from occipitoparietal electrodes as early as ~50 ms after stimulus onset, independently of low-level features such as convex hull, density, individual and total item area. Spatial arrangement was represented later, from ~150 ms, and perceived numerosity, biased by symmetry-induced grouping, emerged at a similar latency. These results indicate that early neural signals encode physical numerosity directly, whereas the symmetry-induced underestimation arises from late grouping processes, such as those involved in incremental grouping, supporting object segmentation.

title: Development of the CRS-7: psychometric properties and percentile reference values for a brief life-course measure of cognitive reserve.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Cognitive reserve (CR) is the capacity of cognitive processes and brain networks to maintain cognitive functioning despite aging, brain pathology or damage through efficiency, flexibility, and compensatory mechanisms. Existing life-course CR questionnaires are often lengthy and burdensome. This study developed a short form of the Cognitive Reserve Scale (CRS-7), examined its preliminary psychometric properties, and generated empirical percentile reference values. A total of 587 adults aged 18-89 years completed the Italian CRS. Scores were averaged across the life stages available to each participant. Exploratory factor analysis identified the CRS-7 item set. Internal consistency was assessed with Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Associations with the original CRS and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) were examined. A two one-sided tests (TOST) procedure tested mean-score equivalence, and sample percentiles were derived. The data were suitable for factor analysis (KMO=0.75; Bartlett's test, p<.001). A seven-item, one-factor solution accounted for 31.60% of variance and showed acceptable internal consistency (alpha=0.75; omega=0.76). CRS-7 scores correlated strongly with the original CRS (r=.73, p<.001) and moderately with MoCA scores (rho=0.42, p<.001). TOST supported equivalence of mean scores within prespecified bounds. Empirical percentile reference values were generated for CRS-7 total scores. The CRS-7 is a promising brief life-course measure of CR that may reduce respondent burden while retaining convergence with the original instrument. Results support its feasibility and provide evidence of internal consistency and convergence with the original CRS, alongside preliminary evidence of a one-factor structure.

title: Quantitative biochemical profiling of GCase activity and α-synuclein proteoforms in post-mortem human brains from GBA-related and idiopathic Parkinson's disease.
authors: van de Berg Wilma D J
abstract: Variants in GBA1, encoding lysosomal glucocerebrosidase (GCase), are risk factors for Parkinson's disease (PD), which is characterized by α-synuclein (αSyn) accumulation and lysosomal dysfunction. Nonetheless, the relationship between αSyn accumulation and GCase deficiency remains unclear. This study aims to quantitatively define the biochemical relationship between GCase and αSyn in GBA-related PD (GBA-PD) and idiopathic PD (IPD). Here, we sequenced GBA1 in 160 post-mortem brains (25 iLBD, 114 PD, 21 controls) and conducted quantitative biochemical analysis of the locus coeruleus (LC), substantia nigra (SN) and gyrus temporalis medius (GTM). We measured Total, Ser129-phosphorylated (pSer129), and C-terminally-truncated αSyn proteoforms, and quantified GCase activity and protein levels. GBA1 variants were detected in 21.9% of PD cases, including a novel frameshift variant. Cortical and midbrain αSyn burden did not differ between GBA-PD and IPD. Importantly, GCase activity and protein levels were substantially reduced in both GBA-PD and IPD across regions, while GCase specific activity was reduced only in the GBA-PD group. pSer129 αSyn burden was inversely correlated with GCase activity, both in the presence (GBA-PD) and absence (IPD) of GBA1 variants. These findings demonstrate a biochemical link between pSer129-enriched αSyn deposition and GCase deficiency across the PD spectrum, supporting lysosomal/GCase-enhancing therapies regardless of GBA1 status.

title: Neuroprotective effects of metformin on cognition, mTOR, and inflammatory cytokines in a scopolamine-induced cognitive impairment model in ovariectomized rats.
abstract: Metformin, with its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties, exhibits protective activity on the central nervous system (CNS). This study examined metformin's impact on anxiety-related cognitive deficits and hippocampal level of cytokines in Alzheimer's (AD)-like and ovariectomized rats. Eighty female Wistar rats were divided into eight groups: control, sham, ovariectomy (ovx), scopolamine (sco), ovariectomy +scopolamine (ovx + sco), metformin + scopolamine (met + sco), metformin + ovariectomy (met + ovx), and metformin + ovariectomy + scopolamine (met + ovx+sco). Morris Water Maze (MWM), Elevated Plus Maze (EPM) tests, Nissl and Thioflavin staining, ELISA, and Western Blot were used. In all groups, Metformin was administered before intraperitoneal injection of scopolamine and before ovariectomy surgery.MWM behavioral test results showed that metformin improved spatial memory in impaired groups (SCO, OVX + SCO and OVX). The EPM behavioral test indicated that metformin could improve the increased anxiety levels found in the impaired groups. Nissl staining revealed the neuronal damage in the rats of the impaired group. Thioflavin staining showed that metformin reduced the number of beta-amyloid plaques in the treatment groups. ELISA results demonstrated increased the levels of cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) in the impaired groups, and metformin reduced these levels. Western blot results showed increased mTOR expression in the affected groups, which metformin was able to reduce. The results indicated that metformin administration prior to intraperitoneal scopolamine injection and ovariectomy surgery was associated with improved learning and spatial memory, reduced anxiety and inflammatory cytokine levels and decreased mTOR expression.

title: Heparan sulfate sulfatases are essential for the patterning of human stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons.
abstract: Midbrain dopaminergic neurons (mDA) are selectively lost in Parkinson's disease, driving sustained efforts to generate bona fide mDA neurons from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) for replacement therapy. While morphogen gradients and transcription factors have been extensively studied, extracellular regulators remain largely overlooked. Here, we identify the heparan sulfate-modifying enzymes SULF1 and SULF2 as essential for establishing mDA neuron identity in vitro. Using CRISPR/Cas9-engineered iPSCs, we show that loss of SULF1/2 increases 6-O-sulfated heparan sulfate species and disrupts patterning both at the anteroposterior and dorsoventral axes in human iPSC-derived mDA cultures. Double-knockout cells thus fail to acquire ventral midbrain fates and instead adopt hindbrain, spinal cord and neural crest-like identities as revealed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Mechanistically, we partially explain the changed patterning to aberrant FGF signaling and demonstrate that FGF inhibition redirects cells toward midbrain fates, however without restoring ventral identity. These findings establish a critical role for SULF1/2 in mDA neuron in vitro differentiation and uncover a previously unrecognized layer of extracellular control over neural patterning.

title: Advances in spinal cord injury therapeutics: integrating foundational research and clinical innovation.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating condition causing profound neurological deficits and significant global burden. Poor functional recovery stems from the limited regenerative capacity of adult central nervous system neurons and a post-injury inhibitory microenvironment featuring scars and molecular inhibitors. Recent multidisciplinary advances offer promising therapeutic avenues. Advanced multi-omics technologies provide unprecedented insights into spinal cord development and injury responses, revealing cellular heterogeneity and molecular dynamics. Progress in stem cell biology, functional biomaterials for lesion bridging and drug/cell delivery, spinal cord tissue engineering and physical neuromodulation techniques enables novel strategies to enhance regeneration and remodel the injury site. Clinical studies also show incremental progress. This review synthesizes foundational biology, pathophysiology, and these converging engineering and biological approaches, aiming to accelerate the development of effective regenerative therapies for SCI repair.

title: Eliminating serum dependency of bovine mesenchymal stem cell expansion via media composition and genetic screen.
abstract: The advancement of cultured fat toward viable industrial production is currently hindered by economic and technical constraints, including the formulation of cost-effective, chemically defined culture media. This study addresses serum dependency in bovine mesenchymal stem cells (bMSCs), a common cell source for cellular agriculture, and particularly for cultured fat given their well-characterized adipogenic potential. We show that while supplementing reduced-serum media with insulin-transferrin-selenium-BSA (ITS+) and fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) mitigates short-term viability loss, these factors fail to sustain prolonged proliferation in serum-free media. To uncover the molecular barriers to serum-free adaptation, we performed a targeted CRISPR-Cas9 screen, identifying TP53 as the primary checkpoint restricting survival. Targeted TP53 disruption conferred a robust survival advantage, enabling long-term expansion in serum-free conditions. By contrast, PTEN knockout displayed an intermediate phenotype, improving viability relative to wild-type cells but falling short of the proliferative capacity achieved by TP53 ablation. Furthermore, we demonstrated that mitigating proteolytic stress using soybean trypsin inhibitor is essential for effective serum-free subculturing. These findings establish that p53 pathway disruption decouples adipose-derived bMSCs (Ad-bMSCs) expansion from serum dependency, offering a scalable strategy for chemically defined fat production.

title: A cumulative polyeXposure score to predict early adolescent substance use based on environmental exposures.
abstract: Early substance use onset is a critical public health issue linked to heightened risks of dependence, psychiatric comorbidities, and overdose later in life. While genetic predispositions are well-studied, the cumulative environmental impact, particularly during the vulnerable developmental window of adolescence, remains poorly quantified. This study analyzed 9771 youth from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development cohort (ages 9-15) and utilized the Exposome-Wide Association Study to derive a data-driven Time-to-Substance-Use PolyeXposure Score (T2SU-PXS) that quantifies environmental liability for substance use risk, and to compare its predictive performance with that of family history density of substance use and a polygenic score for addiction risk. Here we identify six key environmental factors associated with T2SU, including youth behaviors, home environment, and peer and community influences. The T2SU PXS outperforms both family history density of substance use and a polygenic score for addiction risk. The T2SU-PXS represents a crucial methodological advancement in operationalizing the environmental exposome in developmental psychiatry. Its scalability, interpretability, and robustness suggest practical applications in early risk stratification and preventive intervention. By enabling a more comprehensive and context-sensitive understanding of adolescent substance use vulnerability, this integrative exposomic framework may mitigate health disparities in environmentally burdened communities.

title: Warning label compliance of recreationally available cannabis flower and concentrate products in the state of Colorado.
abstract: As rates of cannabis use and recreational access increase, it is imperative that recreational cannabis products have clear, consistent, and standardized labeling practices. The current study assessed labeling accuracy for standardized labeling requirements of 480 (n = 277 flower; n = 203 concentrate) recreational cannabis products purchased from across Colorado. Each product label was assessed for the presence of the following required regulatory components: universal symbol, driving warnings, pregnancy warnings, expiration dates, ideal storage conditions, and THC potency. Observed compliance with warning labels was compared to expected proportions for each regulatory labeling component, and Chi-square was used to assess if these observed proportions were different between cannabis flower and concentrate products. Only the universal symbol met the expected proportion by being present on 99.2% of all product labels. Driving warnings (97.5%), pregnancy warnings (97.5%), expiration dates (51.2%), and ideal storage conditions (16.9%) failed to meet the expected proportions (p's < 0.05). Further, there were differences by product type, with concentrate products being more likely to contain expiration dates and ideal storage conditions compared to flower products (p's < 0.05). Finally, there were differences by product type in THC reporting language, with concentrates being more likely to use "Total THC" and flower products more likely to use "THC" or "Total THC and THC" (p's < 0.05). These results highlight discrepancies in recreational cannabis product labeling practices, and these discrepancies vary by product type. This highlights potential public health, safety, and consumer trust issues that may arise from inconsistent labeling practices of recreational cannabis products.

title: Neural subspaces encode sequential working memory without detectable neural sequences.
abstract: The neural mechanisms of multiple-item working memory are not well understood. In the current study, we address two competing hypotheses about the neural basis of sequential working memory: neural subspaces versus neural sequences. Using broadband MEG data from human participants, we applied dimensionality reduction and multivariate decoding techniques to test whether a sequence of items is maintained through the reactivation of individual items in sequence (neural sequences) or by organizing them into distinct low-dimensional subspaces (neural subspaces). Our results revealed behaviorally relevant, low-dimensional neural subspaces that organized memory representations according to ordinal position in the sequence, supporting the neural subspaces hypothesis. In contrast, we found no evidence of sequential neural replay during the retention period, contrary to the neural sequences hypothesis. In this work, we show that sequential working memory is maintained through structured geometric organization in low-dimensional representational space, rather than through the sequential reactivation of individual items, thus clarifying the mechanisms of multi-item working memory.

title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability.
abstract: Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34-Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.

title: A synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission.
abstract: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural-metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

title: Mitochondria-ER contact sites in neurodegeneration: a homeostatic hub linking metabolic stress, neuroinflammation, and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) involve self-amplifying interactions among proteotoxic stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. Emerging evidence increasingly implicates mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites (MERCs) as dynamic homeostatic hubs that may link these processes, but their causal status in human NDDs remains incompletely established. This review synthesizes evidence connecting MERCs biology with NDD-associated mitochondrial stress, Ca2+ dysregulation, lipid remodeling, redox signaling, and inflammatory cell death. We frame the MERCs-centered model as a working, testable hypothesis and use Eleutherococcus senticosus as a case study for candidate phytochemical modulation of MERCs-associated stress pathways. Available cellular, animal, and human-tissue evidence suggests that altered MERCs structure and function can contribute to mitochondrial Ca2+ overload, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, mtDNA/DAMP release, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Natural products may influence this network indirectly through mitochondrial metabolism, membrane composition, ER stress, redox buffering, and regulated Ca2+ handling, but direct proof of MERCs restoration remains limited. MERCs should be viewed as a convergent homeostatic hub and therapeutic hypothesis rather than a validated upstream cause of NDDs. Future studies should distinguish structural contact-site changes from functional correction and should test phytochemical candidates using direct MERCs proximity, flux, lipidomics, and bioenergetic assays.

title: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine-bound aptamer complex.
abstract: Aptamers are oligonucleotides that have been selected to bind a particular target. Despite the growing popularity of functional DNA aptamers, there remains limited knowledge of their binding mechanisms, as few have been characterized at the atomic level. Here, we use NMR spectroscopy to obtain structural details of RKEC1, a shortened version of a DNA aptamer previously reported to bind dopamine. We find that RKEC1 forms a compact structure upon ligand binding that lacks any Watson-Crick duplex regions or G-quadruplex core, in stark contrast to nearly all predicted and observed DNA aptamer folds. The atomic details explain dopamine specificity amongst structurally similar compounds, and the determined DNA fold was used to guide biosensor design. The aptamer structure further suggests that DNA folding can access an extensive conformational landscape reminiscent of RNA, thus expanding the diversity traditionally captured by predictive algorithms.

title: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BD1 restores neurotransmitter homeostasis in chronic restraint stress mice via tryptophan metabolic reprogramming.
abstract: Psychological stress is a major precipitating factor for neuropsychiatric disorders, and the gut-brain axis has emerged as a critical regulator of mood and behavior, but how specific commensal microbes modulate host neurochemistry to confer stress resilience is largely unknown. In this study, we found that chronic restraint stress-induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in mice are associated with intestinal microbial imbalance and impaired colonic synthesis of 5-HTP, the direct precursor of serotonin. Concurrently, this leads to reduced serotonin levels both systemically and in the CNS, as well as decreased BDNF in the hippocampus. Notably, supplementation with B. animalis BD1 restored the abundance of beneficial Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus as well as colonic 5-HTP levels, thereby normalizing serotonin and BDNF expression in the brain, and ultimately ameliorating depression-like behavior in CRS mice. In addition, we found that BD1 influenced synaptic plasticity and the expression level of the microglial surface marker Iba1 in CRS mice. Our findings reveal a key potential possible course of action: B. animalis BD1 rebalances the disturbed gut microbiota, thereby regulating host intestinal tryptophan metabolism, which in turn buffers depression-like behavior in mice under chronic restraint stress.

title: Clinical characterization and baseline immune correlates of immune checkpoint inhibition-induced neurotoxicity.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-induced neurotoxicity (N-Tox) can be associated with severe symptoms, yet it remains grossly understudied compared to other immune related adverse events (irAEs). We analyzed irAEs of melanoma patients enrolled in three phase III clinical trials (Checkmate 238, 915 and 067), treated with ipilimumab, nivolumab, or ipilimumab and nivolumab. N-Tox was classified by its clinical phenotype and severity. In subsets of patients with available biospecimens, baseline serum autoantibody (aAb) profiling and bulk RNA sequencing of peripheral CD4+ and CD8+ T cells were conducted to determine if baseline host immune response is associated with N-Tox development. Overall, grade ≥ 2 N-Tox occurred in 187 of 1,553 (12%) patients (Grade 2 n = 148, Grade 3 n = 35, and Grade 4 n = 4). Majority of the patients (80%) developed N-Tox within the first 6 months, and 59 (32%) developed multiple N-Tox symptoms. Grade ≥ 2 N-Tox was preceded by lower grade neurologic symptoms in 63 (34%) patients, and 23 (12%) patients required hospitalization. In a multivariable logistic regression analysis using nivolumab as reference, ipilimumab was associated with higher odds of N-Tox (OR = 1.67, p = 0.01), while COMBO was not significant (OR = 1, p = 0.98). N-Tox was associated with lower recurrence rates (OR = 0.74, p = 0.02) and greater clinical benefit of treatment (OR = 2.55, p < 0.0001). Baseline serum aAb profiles in patients who developed N-Tox showed enrichment of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative pathways compared to patients with other grade ≥ 2 irAEs. Gene expression analyses of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells supported these findings, identifying neurodevelopment, neurotransmitter signaling, and synaptic function pathways associated with grade ≥ 2 N-Tox. These findings underscore the importance of early monitoring of ICI-treated patients for N-Tox, including low grade N-Tox. Our results also point to a pre-existing neurotropic contexture that may predispose some patients to N-Tox.

title: Therapeutic targeting of microglial hexokinase-2 attenuates inflammasome activation and improves functional recovery after traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) initiates a secondary inflammatory cascade in which sustained microglial activation contributes to neurological dysfunction. Because inflammatory microglial states are accompanied by bioenergetic reconfiguration, modulation of metabolic regulators may provide a strategy to limit post-traumatic inflammation while preserving essential immune functions. Hexokinase-2 (HK2), a glycolytic enzyme with additional roles in mitochondrial and inflammatory signaling, regulates microglial activation in neurodegenerative conditions; however, its contribution to TBI remains unclear. We investigated HK2 in a mouse model of severe controlled cortical impact (CCI), characterized by extensive ipsilateral cortical damage and involvement of the underlying hippocampus. HK2 expression was assessed at 3, 7, and 15 days post-injury. The HK2 function was targeted pharmacologically with lonidamine (LND; 50 mg/kg, intraperitoneally), administered once daily for 7 days beginning 24 h after CCI, and genetically using a microglial-specific HK2-haplodeficient mouse to produce partial HK2 reduction in microglia. Cortical HK2 mRNA was increased by 3 days post-CCI and remained elevated through day 15, when increased HK2 immunoreactivity was detected in IBA1-positive cells. In vitro, LND restrained acute LPS-induced increases in glycolytic and oxidative activity, reduced total ATP production, and suppressed NF-κB reporter activity. LND also slowed proliferation of microglial-like BV2 cells without impairing uptake of labeled dead-cell cargo. In vivo, LND improved rotarod performance without altering general locomotor activity or spatial working-memory performance and reduced inflammasome-associated gene expression and ASC accumulation, with prominent effects in the hippocampus and hilus. Partial genetic reduction of microglial HK2 similarly improved motor performance after CCI, supporting a contribution of HK2 to post-traumatic dysfunction. Together, these findings identify HK2 as a regulator of microglial bioenergetic and inflammatory responses after severe TBI. Partial HK2 antagonism limits sustained post-traumatic inflammation and is associated with improved functional outcome, supporting further investigation of HK2 modulation as a therapeutic strategy for secondary brain injury.

title: Cultural adaptation, expert validation, and mixed-methods pilot evaluation of a psychologically informed, audiologist-delivered, manualised intervention for tinnitus-related distress in Malaysia.
abstract: Tinnitus disorder entails a significant psychological component, yet it is traditionally managed by audiologists. Due to a lack of specialist mental health providers capable of meeting tinnitus patients' needs, interest is growing in audiologist-delivered, psychologically informed interventions, primarily in Western countries. While such approaches remain limited in low- and middle-income countries, this study aimed to culturally adapt a UK-developed intervention for Malaysian adults with tinnitus and evaluate its validity, preliminary outcomes, and acceptability. The study comprised three stages: (1) translation and cultural adaptation guided by established frameworks; (2) expert review by seven audiologists using face and content validity indices; and (3) a single-arm convergent mixed-methods pilot involving ten adults with chronic tinnitus. Participants received three individual sessions over approximately one month, delivered by a trained audiologist. Tinnitus Functional Index and Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-42 scores were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and three-month follow-up. Missing outcomes were handled using baseline observation carried forward, with completer sensitivity analyses. Acceptability was explored among completers using semi-structured interviews guided by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. All face-validity items and 60 chapter-domain content-validity assessments achieved an index of 1.00. Six of ten participants completed the intervention and all follow-up assessments. In the all-enrolled analysis, mean Tinnitus Functional Index scores decreased from 59.50 at baseline to 40.20 post-intervention and 36.80 at follow-up, with a significant effect of time (p = .011). Depression, anxiety, and stress scores did not change significantly. Among completers, acceptability ratings and qualitative feedback were generally favourable, although some participants described effort associated with practising intervention strategies. The four participants who discontinued provided no observed post-baseline outcome or acceptability data. The culturally adapted intervention demonstrated strong face and content validity, while the pilot showed preliminary favourable outcome patterns and acceptability among completers. However, the small single-arm sample, 40% discontinuation, and absence of acceptability data from participants who discontinued limit interpretation. These findings support further controlled feasibility evaluation of the adapted intervention in Malaysia.

title: A systematic review of substance use disorder methylome-wide association studies in postmortem human brain.
abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) are complex psychiatric conditions influenced by genetic and environmental factors. DNA methylation (DNAm), a dynamic and context-dependent epigenetic mechanism, can offer insight into regulatory variation associated with SUDs, particularly when examined in brain regions central to addiction-related neurobiology. In this systematic review, we compiled findings from 20 methylome-wide association studies (MWASs) of SUDs in postmortem human brain tissue, encompassing alcohol (nstudy=9), opioids (nstudy=4), cocaine (nstudy=3), nicotine (nstudy=2), methamphetamine (nstudy=1), and any illicit drug (nstudy=1). Studies varied in brain regions analyzed, methylation platforms used, and sample characteristics. Most focused on methylation at cytosines followed by guanine (i.e., mCGs). Despite methodological heterogeneity and limited overlap of findings within individual substances, consistent biological themes emerged across substances, including differential methylation in genes related to neurodevelopment, inflammatory response, signaling, and transcriptional regulation. Cross-substance comparisons revealed 525 genes implicated across independent results from at least two substances, suggesting shared methylomic signals that may reflect common neurobiological pathways, downstream adaptations to exposure, or unmeasured polysubstance use. Exploratory drug repurposing analyses based on genes overlapping three or more substances identified a small number of existing compounds with potential relevance for treating polysubstance use. This review synthesizes current results to highlight both the promise and challenges of SUD MWASs in human brain, including limited sample size, generalizability, cell-type specificity, and lack of functional validation. Future research should prioritize multi-omic integration, larger and more diverse cohorts, and advanced technologies to enhance mechanistic understanding and translational potential.

title: Physical fitness in youth and musculoskeletal disease 40 years later - a matched twin study.
abstract: To estimate associations between different physical fitness measures in adolescence and later chronic musculoskeletal disease (MSK) after controlling for genetics and early life environment in twin pairs. In 13 090 male twins born between 1951 and 1978 who underwent conscription examination in Sweden, we studied the association between body mass index (BMI), cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), muscle strength and blood pressure and risk of new onset MSK (specialist or in-patient diagnosis of osteoarthritis, back pain, myalgia, shoulder lesions, join pain) from year 1987 until 2024 using Cox regression, non-stratified (age-adjusted) vs. stratified on twin pairs. The latter models were by-design adjusted for genetics and early life exposures. We also controlled for individual-level education, occupational load, smoking and physical activity level. The mean (SD) age was 18 (0.5) years. 4435 twins developed MSK during the follow-up time. In non-stratified Cox, CRF, muscle strength but not blood pressure were associated with higher risk of MSK (Hazard Ratio, HR = 1.16 per 50 W, 95% confidence interval, CI = 1.11-1.21, HR = 1.08 (1.04-1.11) per 300 N and HR = 0.95 (0.91-0.99, respectively per 10 mmHg). However, in stratified Cox (adjusted for family factors), these associations attenuated (HR = 1.01 (0.87-1.18), HR = 0.98 (0.86-1.11) and HR = 1.00 (0.88-1.13), respectively). Only BMI had a consistent association with MSK in both non-stratified (HR = 1.42 (1.34-1.51) per 5 kg) and stratified (HR = 1.32 (1.03-1.71)) models. Results were similar when we additionally adjusted for leisure physical activity (only available for a subsample). Keeping a low body mass during adolescence was associated with a lower risk of joint and muscle diseases up to 40 years later. This potential life-lasting benefit stands regardless of genetics, childhood environment, education level and occupational load as well as physical fitness or activity levels in adolescence.

title: Needs assessment of medical curricula development for patients with physical, intellectual, and/or developmental disabilities or non-english language preferences.
abstract: Individuals with physical, intellectual, and developmental disabilities (P/IDD) and those with non-English language preferences (NELP) experience significant health disparities, which have been traced to inadequacies in medical training. There is a need to create inclusive national standardized medical curricula by examining the curricular priorities in small-scale examples for implementation. 32 medical students at a community-founded and student-centered medical school participated in an open-ended survey and curricular priorities were identified. Curricular priorities for P/IDD patients were understanding diverse clinical presentations, care for disabled adults, and transitioning into adulthood. For NELP patients, priorities were increasing representation of minority physicians, navigating care for unfamiliar cultures, and help with government services. Medical students emphasized a need for P/IDD and NELP-specific using video lectures and hands-on practical experience.

title: Context-dependent localization and expression of glutamate and GABA and their machinery in microglia.
abstract: Microglia are central regulators of brain homeostasis and synaptic architecture, but whether they, like astrocytes, act as reservoirs and handlers of glutamate and GABA is unknown. Using post-embedding immunogold electron microscopy, we provide the first ultrastructural evidence that individual microglial processes contain GABA and glutamate. At the nanoscale, glutamate-positive microglial processes were preferentially apposed to glutamatergic terminals, whereas GABA-positive processes showed no consistent spatial relationship to GABAergic boutons. At the microscale, spatial transcriptomics revealed that microglial somata expressing GABA-handling genes are enriched in GABAergic neuron-rich regions, while microglia expressing glutamate-handling genes are enriched in glutamatergic neuron-rich regions. Analysis of four single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets (6,594,428 cells, including 320,683 microglia) demonstrated conserved expression of glutamate and GABA transport and metabolism genes in microglia across species, corroborated at the protein level by proteomics and in situ by confocal microscopy. Functionally, acute neuroinflammation selectively depleted microglial GABA content by 57% while leaving glutamate unchanged, indicating differential vulnerability of these amino acid pools. Together, these multimodal data identify microglia as previously unrecognized reservoirs of the brain's principal inhibitory and excitatory transmitters, with spatially adapted handling machinery, and implicate them as potential contributors to excitation-inhibition homeostasis within the quad-partite synapse.

title: Clostridioides difficile colitis promotes neuroinflammatory responses in the prefrontal cortex: a preclinical study in mice.
abstract: Recurrent and severe Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a significant problem in the elderly. There is growing evidence that intestinal dysbiosis and inflammation, characteristic features of CDI, can influence brain function.
