We examined whether neuroinflammatory responses occur during CDI and employed a spatial metabolomic and transcriptomic approach, integrated with biomolecular analyses, to characterize these responses in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) of a CDI mouse model. 6-month-old mice were infected with C. difficile and euthanized on days 3, 4, and 7 post-infection (p.i.) for spatial metabolic analysis, bulk RNA-sequencing of the PFC, or systemic and gut inflammation analysis. Infected mice developed diarrhea and weight loss that peaked by day 3 and resolved by day 7. Spatial metabolomics analysis of the infected brain tissues indicated an imbalance of various neuroprotective metabolites in the PFC on day 4. Differential gene expression analysis identified 124 differentially expressed genes on day 7. Gene set enrichment analysis identified upregulation of pathways associated with neurodegenerative diseases and oxidative phosphorylation in infected mice. PFC protein and transcripts levels of GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein) were increased in infected mice, indicating a reactive astrocyte response. Increased levels of lipocalin-2 (Lcn2), myeloperoxidase (MPO), calprotectin (S100A8/A9), IL-33, and IL-13 were also found in the PFC of infected mice. Levels of fecal Lcn2, a marker of intestinal epithelial barrier disruption, correlate positively with the levels of Lcn2, MPO, and S100A8/A9 in the PFC. Our findings show that CDI, in a mouse model, induces metabolomic and transcriptomic changes in the PFC, including genes associated with oxidative phosphorylation and neurodegeneration.

title: MiR-182 regulates IL-6 and HCN4 in the cardiac context: implications for human atrial electrical remodelling.
abstract: The progression of cardiac electrical remodelling and the onset of proarrhythmic events are multifactorial processes, with many factors contributing to atrial electrical remodelling and the consequent development of atrial fibrillation (AF). Recently, miR-182 has been identified as causative factors of arrhythmogenesis in animal models but its potential relationship with proinflammatory mediators such as interleukin-6 (IL-6), emerged as new key player in independent preclinical evidence for atrial electrogenesis, remains unknown. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) were differentiated into cardiomyocytes (CMs) to study the role of miR-182-overexpression (OE) in human cardiac background. Functional consequences were assessed by measuring spontaneous electrical activity by using MULTIPLE-High-Throughput and Intracell systems, with/without autonomic stimulation. Molecular analyses by RT-PCR/Elisa assays were performed. Hearts from the Tg(myl7:GAL4,EGFP)xTg(Sce.4xUAS: miR-182,cry: EGFP) zebrafish line [Tg(myl7 > miR-182)] were used to measure the expression of dre-il6. Human IL-6 protein (5,4 pg/nL) was microinjected in the pericardial region of 2dpf Tg(myl7:EGFP) wt-like zebrafish embryos and heart rate was recorded. Expression analyses were performed on human left atrial samples of 49 patients (11 controls, CT; 18 left atrial dilation (LA-D); 20 permanent AF). MiR-182-OE in hiPS-CMs significantly impact cardiac electrophysiology showing reduced and irregular spontaneous beating rate. Accordingly, MiR-182-OE downregulated the expression of HCN4, encoding for the pacemaker f-current, incrementing IL-6 expression and secretion and via ISL1. On the contrary, 24-48 h incubation with IL-6 (50ng/mL) did not change miR-182-5p expression levels in CT hiPS-CMs. The IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab (TOC, 10 µg/mL) partially rescued HCN4 expression in miR-182-OE hiPS-CMs. Interestingly, miR-182-OE in hiPS-CMs enhanced response to acetylcholine and dysregulated genes associated with atrial pathology. Zebrafish heart samples from Tg(myl7 > miR-182) exhibited increased il6 expression levels. Pericardial injection of human IL-6 in wt zebrafish embryos decreased heart rate. Finally, miR-182-5p was found to be overexpressed in human biopsies from patients with LA-D, with the highest expression levels observed in patients with permanent AF; remarkably, miR-182 levels were positively correlated with IL-6 expression. The results support the hypothesis of a causative link between miR-182-OE and IL-6 production in the cardiac context. This molecular axis may represent an associated molecular signature predisposing to arrhythmogenesis. Overall, our findings reveal novel pathophysiological mechanisms concordant across models and suggest novel pharmacological targets within the complex AF setting.

title: Development and evaluation of an Android-based platform for early MCI screening in an elderly population.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an intermediate stage of cognitive decline fitting between normal cognition and dementia. With the growing aging population, this study aimed to develop and psychometrically validate an Android-based application for early MCI screening in elderly subjects. This study was conducted in two phases, including the initial design and prototyping of the application named M-Check, and the psychometric evaluation of the app. Face validity was determined by two checklists provided to the expert panel and the elderly subjects. Convergent validity of the M-Check app was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) battery through Pearson correlation. Test-retest and internal consistency and reliability were evaluated using InterClass Correlation (ICC) and Kuder-Richardson coefficients, respectively. In addition, the usability was assessed by a System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire. SPSS 16.0 was employed to analyze the data. The app's usability assessment by the elderly and experts scored 77.11 and 82.5, respectively. Also, the correlation showed that the M-Check app was negatively correlated with the MoCA test (r = -0.71, p < 0.05), and the ICC was more than 0.7. Moreover, the Kuder-Richardson coefficient was 0.82, corresponding to an acceptable reliability. In this study, we validated the M-Check app for MCI screening based on the growing need for mobile-based cognitive assessment tools. Such screeners are expected to take much shorter times than typical neuropsychological batteries do. Additional work is needed to ensure that M-Check is ready for use without the presence of a trained person.

title: Patient depressive symptoms and reciprocity are associated with distress in the caregiver of patients with migraine: insights from the MI-DEAR observational cohort study.
journal: The journal of headache and pain
abstract: As awareness of migraine disability is becoming higher, the recognition of the pivotal role of caregivers of people with migraine and their burden is still scarce. We aimed to investigate the factors associated with the distress of informal caregivers of patients affected by high-frequency or chronic migraine with depressive symptoms. All consecutive adult patients with high-frequency or chronic migraine and depressive symptoms were considered, along with their caregivers. Sociodemographic characteristics and the average weekly hours spent together were assessed among patients and their caregivers (dyads). In patients, we evaluated monthly migraine days (MMDs), monthly acute medications (MAMs), pain intensity, migraine-related disability, the composite 4D score on migraine burden, and depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9-PHQ-9). Caregivers filled in the Relative Stress Scale (RSS). The mutuality scale (MS) was also collected in the dyads. 154 dyads (308 participants) were enrolled (patients aged 42.6 years, SD 12.7; 80.5% female; and their caregivers aged 48.1 years, SD 12.2; 36.4% female). The mean shared reported time was 89.7, SD 29.7 h per week. In patients, PHQ-9 scores were higher in those with higher disability scores (MIDAS; p < 0.001), whereas MMDs were not directly related (p = 0.356). The RSS score in caregivers was 20.6 (SD 10.9). Among caregivers' features, the reciprocity subdomain of the MS was inversely related (p = 0.009) to the perceived distress (RSS). The MS total scores and subdomains (p consistently < 0.05) were highly related within the dyad. A positive, mild relation was observed between caregiver RSS and patient PHQ-9 (r = 0.197; p = 0.014) and 4D (r = 0.234; p = 0.004) scores. Finally, when both caregiver and patient characteristics were included, the caregiver reciprocity MS subdomain (p < 0.001) was the main factor associated with RSS scores. The MI-DEAR study highlighted the elevated perceived distress of caregivers of hard-to-treat patients with migraine and depressive symptoms. Low caregiver reciprocity, more severe patients' depressive symptoms, and multidimensional migraine burden were associated with higher caregivers' distress. The study was preregistered on clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07029126 on Jun 11th 2025.

title: Screening identifies food-derived Limosilactobacillus reuteri candidates with distinct metabolic benefits in diet-induced obesity.
abstract: Food-derived bacteria represent a potential source of strains with distinct metabolic phenotypes. In this study, 29 Clostridium butyricum and 72 Limosilactobacillus reuteri isolates were recovered from 20 non-industrially processed food samples collected across China and classified into 26 and 22 random amplified polymorphic DNA (RAPD) genotypes, respectively. The isolates were evaluated for post-stress growth recovery under simulated gastrointestinal challenges, metabolite production, antimicrobial activity, cell-surface properties, and preliminary phenotypic safety. The retained C. butyricum isolates produced 1.98-4.85 g/L butyrate from glucose and 2.36-4.35 g/L from starch. Reuterin production varied substantially among L. reuteri isolates, with four isolates producing 16.57-49.18 mM and the remaining isolates producing less than 10 mM. Strain 28A2 exhibited 87.64% autoaggregation and comparatively strong inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus. Hierarchical clustering and principal component analysis (PCA) were used to prioritize three C. butyricum and four L. reuteri strains for subsequent evaluation. The four selected L. reuteri strains showed Caco-2 adhesion percentages of 13.95-22.30%. In lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, cell-free extracts from strains 28A2 and 32C1 reduced nitric oxide (NO) production by 48.42% and 17.39%, respectively, and interleukin-6 (IL-6) secretion by 18.38% and 47.08% at 1 mg/mL. Their cell-free supernatants also reduced lipid accumulation in differentiated 3T3-L1 adipocytes. During an 18-week intervention in high-sugar, high-fat (HSHF) mice, strain 28A2 reduced body weight change percentage, final body weight, and area under the curve (AUC) for the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) relative to the HSHF group. Strain 32C1 reduced fasting blood glucose and epididymal fat mass but did not significantly affect final body weight or glucose tolerance. The C. butyricum strains did not significantly affect body weight or fasting blood glucose in a separate 12-week experiment. Taken together, this study characterizes the strain-level phenotypic diversity of food-derived isolates; L. reuteri 28A2 (from Jiangshui sour porridge) and 32C1 (from raw camel milk) represent functionally distinct candidates with endpoint-specific metabolic effects, warranting further comparative benchmarking, genomic safety assessment, and mechanistic exploration.

title: Alcohol cue-induced functional connectivity in rats: effects of age of onset and drinking severity.
abstract: Adolescents' heightened reward sensitivity has been suggested to contribute to increased risky drinking during this developmental period compared to adulthood. However, little is known about how age of onset and drinking severity relate to alcohol cue-reactivity, a potential biomarker of addiction. The present study investigated alcohol cue-induced functional connectivity in rats defined by age of onset (adolescent or adult) and drinking level (low vs. high; LD vs. HD), following two months of intermittent alcohol exposure. Three to six days after alcohol exposure, rats underwent an fMRI olfactory cue-reactivity paradigm, including ethanol, appetitive sugar water and neutral water odour cues. Cue-induced functional connectivity was estimated using trial-wise beta-series correlations. An age effect was observed, with higher medial prefrontal cortex-retrosplenial cortex connectivity for both ethanol > water and ethanol > sugar + water contrasts in adolescent- versus adult-onset rats. However, neither effect met the corrected threshold after adjusting for abstinence duration. No main effects of drinking severity survived correction. However, interactions between age of onset and severity were found. Adolescent-onset HD was associated with reduced prelimbic-anterior cingulate cortex connectivity for ethanol > water compared to LD, while adult-onset LD rats exhibited reduced connectivity compared to adolescent-onset LD rats. Similarly, adolescent-onset HD was associated with reduced amygdala-insula connectivity for ethanol > sugar + water compared to LD and adult-onset HD rats. These interaction effects remained significant after adjusting for abstinence duration. High adolescent-onset alcohol use was associated with reduced prefrontal and limbic connectivity during alcohol cue exposure. These findings suggest that cue-induced functional connectivity may be sensitive to heavy alcohol exposure during adolescence. While effects may reflect developmental differences, alcohol exposure, or both, they highlight adolescence as a potentially sensitive period for differences in neural cue processing.

title: Membrane Lipid Composition and Asymmetry Modulate Translocation Versus Leakage of the Model Amphipathic Peptide MAP.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can enable intracellular access while avoiding cytotoxicity, yet their behavior is highly sensitive to membrane composition. Here we show that lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry act as a switch that determines whether the amphipathic CPP MAP undergoes nondisruptive translocation or stabilizes membrane pores that drive leakage. Using high-field computational electrophysiology (CompEL) simulations in membranes of increasing physiological relevance, we show that electrically induced membrane defects allow the insertion of MAP peptides. We find symmetric anionic bilayers favor MAP insertion coupled to transmembrane pore stabilization in POPC/POPG membranes, reproducing progressive dye release in liposome leakage assays. Incorporation of cholesterol reduces the number of inserted peptides and conducts to faster leakage kinetics in cholesterol-containing vesicles. In contrast, a minimal asymmetric membrane model (POPC extracellular leaflet; POPC/POPS intracellular leaflet) supports MAP translocation without sustained membrane disruption. This delivery-relevant mechanism is supported by efficient MAP internalization in HEK293 cells while maintaining high viability. Polarized ATR-FTIR provides structural context, indicating predominantly membrane-associated α-helical conformations across lipid compositions. Together, these results establish lipid asymmetry and composition as actionable biointerface parameters that tune CPP function between translocation and leakage and demonstrate an experimentally benchmarked framework for predicting membrane outcomes across complex lipid environments.

title: Predictors of outcomes of endoscopic sinus surgery for CRSwNP: a systematic review of the literature.
abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) has a wide spectrum of severity and varying impact on quality of life. Endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) is effective for symptom relief and modifying the natural history of the disease in most patients. Although there have been numerous attempts to ascertain factors predicting outcomes after ESS, there is no universally accepted model for identifying those at risk that can be applied in clinical practice. This systematic review aimed to identify potential pre-, peri- and post-operative factors predicting poor outcomes after ESS. A total of 152 studies were identified for inclusion, revealing a number of factors well predicting poor outcomes: asthma, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug-exacerbated respiratory disease, previous surgery (time from last surgery, involvement of frontal sinus, number of surgeries), severity and duration of symptoms pre-operatively, high pre-operative Lund-Mackay score and high tissue eosinophil counts. Some evidence was also found for allergy, surgical related factors and lack of post-operative use of corticosteroids, high ethmoid-to-maxillary opacification ratios at computed tomography scan, high Lund-Kennedy endoscopic score, osteitis and interleukin-5 as biomarkers. This review may assist clinicians in identifying patients at higher risk of poor outcomes after ESS, contributing to more precise and personalised medical care.

title: MTCL1/2 orchestrates actin and MT dynamics in the Golgi region to regulate secretory trafficking.
abstract: The Golgi apparatus integrates microtubule and actin dynamics to coordinate membrane trafficking and organelle architecture, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying this coordination remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the homologous microtubule-associated proteins MTCL1 and MTCL2 differentially recruit distinct cytoskeletal regulators to orchestrate actin and microtubule dynamics in the Golgi region. MTCL2 specifically interacts with the microtubule-severing enzyme katanin, and they function antagonistically to regulate Golgi-associated microtubule stabilization and organization. Conversely, MTCL1 binds the actin-capping protein CAPZ and recruits it to the Golgi region, promoting localized actin stress fiber assembly and focal adhesion formation. In vitro reconstitution reveals that MTCL1 and MTCL2 stabilize microtubules primarily through their C-terminal microtubule-binding domains, with MTCL2 additionally recruiting katanin and enhancing its severing activity. Functional analyses suggest that these proteins operate within a coordinated katanin-MTCL1/2-CAPZ module, which is critical for establishing cortical docking sites that direct microtubule-based transport and the precise fusion of secretory vesicles.

title: Nationwide Survey and Epidemiology of Huntington's Disease in Hungary.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a rare, autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by a CAG repeat expansion in the HTT gene. Despite its defined genetic basis, epidemiological coverage remains heterogeneous across Europe. The objective of the study was to assess the temporal and regional distribution of genetically confirmed HD cases in Hungary (2003-2021) and the impact of healthcare accessibility and the COVID-19 pandemic on diagnostic activity. We analyzed 480 genetically confirmed patients (217 males, 263 females) with pathogenic HTT expansions (>36 CAG repeats). Diagnostic incidence (per 100,000 person-years) and prevalence (per 100,000 population) were calculated using national demographic data. Associations between CAG repeat length and age at onset were examined, and spatial analyses assessed regional distribution relative to specialized centers. Mean annual diagnostic incidence was 0.32 per 100,000 person-years and prevalence 4.73 per 100,000. Median CAG repeat length was 44 (IQR: 41-47), with median age at onset of 45 years, showing an inverse correlation (R2 = 0.41, p < 0.0001). Diagnostic incidence was within the lower-to-mid European range, while prevalence was comparable to Western Europe. Regional disparities were evident, with 65% of cases within 70 km of tertiary centers. Diagnostic activity declined by ∼25% during the pandemic. Although the genetic and clinical characteristics of HD in Hungary are comparable to other European populations, the observed epidemiological patterns appear to be influenced by healthcare accessibility. Inequitable access to specialized neurological services may affect case identification and diagnostic timing and is likely to contribute to differences in epidemiological estimates in rare neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Penicivirols A-D, Alkenylated Tetrahydropyran Derivatives From the Fungus Penicillium virgatum SZSS 4-3-6.
abstract: Four new alkenylated tetrahydropyran derivatives, penicivirols A-D (1-4), together with three known statins (5-7), were isolated from cultures of the plant endophytic fungus Penicillium virgatum SZSS 4-3-6. Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive NMR spectroscopic analysis. The absolute configurations of 1-4 were assigned by quantum chemical calculations combined with the CP3 statistical method. Compounds 4-6 showed preliminary neuroprotective potential against H2O2-induced damage in SH-SY5Y cells. Compound 5 showed moderate cytotoxicity against BV2 and MCF-7 cells, with IC50 values of 36.25 ± 0.23 µM and 22.67 ± 6.54 µM, respectively. However, none of the compounds displayed significant antimicrobial activity against C. albicans, S. aureus, or E. coli in preliminary screening. Additionally, compounds 1-7 did not inhibit lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in RAW 264.7 cells.

title: Therapeutic Potential of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Stroke Management: Evidence From Bench to Bedside.
abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of global disability, yet no pharmacotherapy has shown consistent neuroprotection. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have emerged as multifaceted therapeutic agents with cerebrovascular and neuroprotective properties. We synthesized evidence from preclinical models, major cardiovascular outcome trials, and real-world registries, evaluating agent-specific heterogeneity by contrasting long-acting and short-acting formulations across metabolic phenotypes. We further integrate multi-dimensional mechanisms beyond glucose lowering, including neuroinflammation modulation via microglial polarization, blood-brain barrier preservation through astrocyte-dependent pathways, and vascular protection via Wnt/β-catenin and Nrf2 signaling. Long-acting GLP-1RAs consistently reduced stroke and major adverse cardiovascular events, with benefit partly independent of glycemic control, while short-acting agents showed a less consistent signal. Preclinically, GLP-1RAs limited infarct volume, edema, and hemorrhagic transformation and preserved barrier integrity through the above pathways. However, these robust functional gains failed to translate into clinical functional endpoints, as trials were powered for incidence and mortality rather than disability. GLP-1RAs represent a paradigm shift in comprehensive stroke management, but the pivotal translational gap persists: clinical endpoints have focused on incidence and mortality while functional benefit remains untested. Rigorously designed phase III trials prioritizing functional recovery, cognitive preservation, and optimal therapeutic windows are urgently needed.

title: Development of a Protocol to Retrospectively Identify Acute Traumatic Brain Injury Using Electronic Medical Records From an Academic Health System Data Warehouse.
abstract: As recommended in the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke TBI Classification and Nomenclature Initiative, retrospective identification of traumatic brain injury (TBI) from electronic medical record (EMR) data offers major potential for research and surveillance. Enterprise data warehouses integrating structured and unstructured EMR data could support this work, yet few studies have evaluated their use for TBI case ascertainment. This study describes a manual chart review protocol to identify acute TBI among patients receiving head computed tomography (CT) scan from a large health system's enterprise data warehouse. We identified encounters potentially related to TBI using clinical documentation files (e.g., Emergency Department Triage, History & Physical, Discharge Summary) within our institution's enterprise data warehouse. Two independent raters applied the protocol to 126 patients who presented in 2019 and underwent head CT. Sampling was limited to patients receiving a head CT scan to enrich the cohort with both TBI and non-TBI cases. We developed a decision tree workflow to guide documentation of a plausible mechanism of head injury accompanied by clinical symptoms and/or clinically indicated neuroimaging. Criteria were adapted from the American Congress of Rehabilitation Medicine definition of mild TBI and modified for retrospective EMR data. Raters classified each case as (1) no evidence of acute TBI, (2) sufficient evidence of acute TBI, or (3) inconclusive evidence due to missing data or confounding conditions (e.g., syncope). Inter-rater reliability demonstrated strong agreement across raters (88.1% agreement; Cohen's κ = 0.80 (95% CI: 0.71-0.89), p < 0.0001); inter-rater reliability was similar across subgroups of age (±65 years), sex, and payor (government/non-government insurance). Among the 126 cases reviewed, there was agreement on sufficient evidence of acute TBI for 49 cases (86.0% agreement between rater 1 and 2), no evidence of acute TBI for 54 cases (96.4% agreement), and inconclusive evidence for 8 cases (61.5% agreement). Sensitivity analyses reweighting the sample to parent cohort marginal distributions for rate of TBI produced similar results (94.2% agreement, κ = 0.74 (95% CI: 0.58-0.90). This manual chart review protocol showed strong inter-rater reliability for identifying acute TBI using EMR data. Future research should examine external reliability in other health systems and compare its performance with International Classification of Diseases-based definitions and prospective diagnosis. As enterprise data warehouses become more ubiquitous, reliable case ascertainment protocols such as this could facilitate standardized, scalable retrospective identification of TBI, supporting retrospective TBI cohort studies.

title: Oral conscious sedation is widely used in paediatric dentistry to reduce anxiety and improve cooperation during diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Although several pharmacological agents are internationally recognised as effective and safe, regulatory restrictions significantly limit the available options in Italy, particularly within private outpatient dental practice.
abstract: Oral conscious sedation is widely used in paediatric dentistry to reduce anxiety and improve cooperation during diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Although several pharmacological agents are internationally recognised as effective and safe, regulatory restrictions significantly limit the available options in Italy, particularly within private outpatient dental practice. A narrative review of the literature was conducted using PubMed from database inception to March 2025. In addition, national and international guidelines, regulatory documents and Italian drug agency databases were consulted to contextualise the regulatory framework. Studies involving paediatric patients (0-18 years) undergoing oral conscious sedation in dental settings were considered. The current Italian regulatory framework substantially restricts pharmacological options for oral conscious sedation in paediatric dentistry. While prioritising patient safety, these limitations create a discrepancy between international evidence and everyday clinical practice. Greater regulatory harmonisation and expanded specialist training pathways may help improve therapeutic flexibility, while maintaining high safety standards.

title: Direct cortical electrical stimulation-induced seizures: Are they reliable? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
abstract: We aimed to assess the frequency, clinical relevance, and prognostic value of stimulation-induced seizures (SIS) during intracranial EEG recording (iEEG), and to compare high-frequency (HF) and low-frequency (LF) stimulation protocols. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting SIS during preoperative iEEG. Pooled proportions of SIS and habitual seizures were estimated using random-effects models. Differences between HF and LF stimulation were assessed using odds ratios. Study-level meta-regression was conducted to evaluate associations between SIS rates, habitual seizure proportions, and postoperative favorable seizure outcome (Engel Ia). Twenty-five studies were included. SIS occurred more frequently with HF than LF stimulation (56.1% vs. 35.8%; OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.50-2.23; p < 0.001), with substantial between-study heterogeneity. Among patients with SIS, LF stimulation was associated with a higher proportion of habitual seizures compared to HF (81.8% vs. 72.9%), although this difference was not statistically significant. A higher proportion of habitual electro-clinical seizures among SIS correlated with increased rates of favorable seizure outcomes with LF stimulation (p = 0.004) but not with HF stimulation (p = 0,912). Finally, MRI-visible lesions and the mesio-temporal seizure-onset zone were associated with higher SIS rates (p < 0.01). In conclusion, HF stimulation increases the likelihood of inducing SIS, but SIS frequency was not associated with a higher proportion of favorable seizure outcomes. Instead, the clinical relevance of SIS depends on their similarity to habitual seizures. These findings suggest that SIS may reflect underlying network excitability, and that their diagnostic value lies in their semiological and EEG concordance rather than occurrence of stimulated seizures alone. Overall, these results emphasize the importance of stimulation-induced habitual electro-clinical seizures for postsurgical outcome prognostication.

title: An Atomically Precise Pyruvate Dehydrogenase-Mimicking Au-Cu Cluster Restores Cerebral Bioenergetics.
abstract: Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) is the indispensable gatekeeper linking glycolysis to mitochondrial oxidation, and its inactivation drives bioenergetic collapse across a range of metabolic and neurodegenerative disorders, yet directly restoring its catalytic function with an artificial enzyme has remained an unmet challenge. Here, through biomimetic electronic structure engineering, we develop an atomically precise Au-Cu cluster that mimics PDH catalytic activity and restores cerebral bioenergetics in vivo. The cluster exhibits PDH-mimicking activity toward pyruvate (Km = 2.19 mM), driving pyruvate oxidation and NAD+ regeneration to reinstate TCA cycle flux, enhance ATP production, and rescue mitochondrial membrane potential under hyperglycemic stress. Remarkably, the Au-Cu cluster crosses the compromised blood-brain barrier, reactivates cerebral PDH activity, and reestablishes metabolic homeostasis in db/db mice. This bioenergetic recovery activates the Sirt1-mitochondrial biogenesis axis, suppresses neuroinflammation, and restores neurological function. Together, this work establishes atomically precise clusters as catalytically active bioenergetic modulators capable of substituting for a native metabolic enzyme in vivo, offering a promising therapeutic paradigm for diabetic cognitive impairment and other bioenergetic disorders.

title: Age-stratified functional outcomes after microsurgical vestibular schwannoma resection in 180 adults: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: The objective of this paper was to evaluate age-stratified functional outcomes after microsurgical resection of sporadic vestibular schwannoma (VS) and to assess the association of age with facial nerve and hearing outcomes within a function-preserving strategy. We analyzed 180 adults who underwent microsurgical VS resection at a single center and summarized outcomes in four prespecified age groups (younger adults, 18-39 years; middle-aged adults, 40-59 years; early older adults, 60-69 years; and older adults, ≥70 years). Primary endpoints were favorable facial nerve function (House-Brackmann [HB] I-II) and serviceable hearing (Gardner-Robertson [GR] I-II) among hearing-preservation candidates (preoperative GR I-II), both assessed at 2-year follow-up. Age was modeled as a continuous predictor using restricted cubic splines adjusted for Hannover tumor extension classification, side, preoperative function, symptom duration and extent of resection. A prespecified sensitivity contrast compared patients aged <60 versus ≥60 years. Secondary outcomes included Karnofsky Performance Status, complications and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay. Two-year HB I-II rates were 95% (38/40), 98.6% (69/70), 88.4% (38/43), and 92.6% (25/27) across the four age groups (overall 94.5%). Among hearing-preservation candidates, serviceable hearing at 2 years was 36.8% (7/19), 45.5% (15/33), 55.6% (10/18) and 50% (4/8), respectively (overall 46.2%). Continuous-age models showed no statistically significant overall or non-linear age effect for either endpoint after adjustment. In the prespecified <60 versus ≥60 sensitivity analysis, patients aged ≥60 years had lower adjusted odds of HB I-II (OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01-0.56; P=0.0129), whereas the hearing contrast was not significant (OR 1.68, 95% CI 0.45-6.27; P=0.4427). ICU length of stay was longer in the ≥70 group. Among carefully selected surgical candidates, age alone should not preclude microsurgical resection of VS when surgery is indicated. Within a function-preserving paradigm, 2-year facial nerve outcomes remained high across age groups and serviceable hearing was achievable in appropriately selected candidates.

title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation for fibromyalgia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Fibromyalgia is a chronic pain syndrome associated with central sensitization, autonomic dysfunction, and neuroimmune dysregulation. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological neuromodulatory intervention targeting pain processing, autonomic balance, and inflammatory pathways. However, evidence regarding its efficacy in fibromyalgia remains limited. To systematically evaluate the efficacy, safety, and potential clinical implications of taVNS in patients with fibromyalgia through qualitative synthesis and meta-analysis. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies evaluating taVNS in fibromyalgia. Primary outcomes included pain reduction, while secondary outcomes comprised functional status, sleep quality, psychological symptoms, autonomic parameters, and safety. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated standardized within-group changes in pain rather than comparative between-group treatment effects. Five studies involving 333 patients fulfilled eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Three studies comprising 100 patients contributed to the quantitative analysis. Meta-analysis demonstrated a large standardized within-group improvement in pain following taVNS-based interventions (Hedges g = 2.75; 95% CI 1.38-4.11). However, substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 91.4%) and the limited number of studies warrant cautious interpretation. Across studies, taVNS-based interventions were associated with improvements in pain intensity, Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire scores, anxiety symptoms, sleep quality, and overall disease burden. Akkurt et al. additionally reported improvements in autonomic parameters. Considerable variability existed in stimulation protocols, treatment duration, comparator groups, and concomitant interventions. Some studies combined taVNS with exercise therapy or pain neuroscience education, limiting attribution of benefits specifically to vagal stimulation. Reported adverse effects were mild, and treatment tolerability was generally favorable. Current evidence suggests that taVNS may provide clinical benefits for patients with fibromyalgia, particularly regarding pain, functional status, psychological symptoms, sleep quality, and autonomic regulation. Nevertheless, small sample sizes, substantial methodological and statistical heterogeneity, concomitant interventions, and limited follow-up preclude definitive conclusions regarding efficacy. Larger, adequately powered, sham-controlled randomized trials employing standardized stimulation protocols and clinically meaningful outcomes are necessary to establish the therapeutic effectiveness of taVNS in fibromyalgia.

title: Reverse Looping for Nerve Repair: An Experimental Study on Retrograde Axonal Regeneration.
Sleep and Mood in Retinitis Pigmentosa.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to identify whether retinitis pigmentosa (RP) has an impact on sleep and mood, and whether disease severity exacerbates this. Eighty-seven patients with an RP phenotype of inherited retinal dystrophy were recruited from Oxford University Hospital NHS Trust. Three hundred three healthy controls were also recruited from the participating centers. Subjective sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Anxiety and depression (e.g. "mood") was quantified using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) and daytime sleepiness using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Mann-Whitney U testing was used for between-group statistical comparisons. Spearman's rho coefficient was used to explore correlations between factors. Individuals with RP had significantly worse global sleep quality (PSQI; P = 0.0375) compared with controls. This was due primarily to altered sleep efficiency (P = 0.0034). Regression analyses of participants with RP suggest the driver for poorer sleep was visual acuity (P = 0.0197), particularly in sleep duration (P = 0.0066). Poor visual acuity significantly correlated with poor rod and cone responses and loss of visual field. However, only decreased visual acuity was significant for poorer sleep. Across all groups, increased PSQI (e.g. worsened sleep) correlated with significantly worsened HADS (r = 0.2755, P < 0.0001). HADS scores were not significantly increased in RP participants versus controls. Our study identified poorer sleep in patients with RP, which correlated with reduced visual acuity. Levels of anxiety and depression were similar between groups.

title: Present and emerging management strategies for chorea in Huntington's disease.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is characterized by a triad of abnormal movements, cognitive dysfunction leading to dementia, and psychiatric disturbance. Chorea, the principal motor manifestation in HD, typically affects all parts of the body. The current treatment of HD remains symptomatic, although many ongoing trials are investigating disease modifying therapies. This narrative review critically evaluates the relevant literature of current management strategies for chorea and emerging therapies undergoing clinical trials where chorea is an endpoint. PubMed was searched from inception to October 2026. Tetrabenazine and other vesicular monoamine transport 2 (VMAT2) inhibitors remain the pharmacological mainstay for chorea management. Antipsychotics may be used to treat comorbid psychiatric or behavioral disturbance, while neurosurgical treatments for HD-related movement dysfunction remain unproven. Novel disease modifying approaches include huntingtin-lowering and gene-silencing approaches, therapies targeting other pathogenic mechanisms, and cell replacement, all of which could reduce chorea if they prove successful. Future HD management is likely to integrate earlier personalized disease modification with phenotype-directed symptomatic treatment. High-quality multidisciplinary care will continue to be a major determinant of quality of life and progression. Even if disease modification succeeds, established chorea may continue to require symptomatic treatment.

title: Subjective Word-Finding Complaints in Older Adults: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of a Novel Self-Reported Questionnaire.
journal: Journal of geriatric psychiatry and neurology
abstract: ObjectivesSubjective word-finding complaints (SWFC) are among the most frequent cognitive complaints in cognitively unimpaired older adults (CU). However, no comprehensive tools currently exist to assess this phenomenon. This study aimed to conduct a preliminary psychometric evaluation of a novel SWFC questionnaire (SWFC-Q), better characterize SWFC, and establish their demographic/clinical correlates.Methods259 French-speaking older adults (174 CU, 85 with mild cognitive impairment (MCI)) from the PREVENT-AD cohort completed a novel 29-item SWFC-Q. Internal (factor) structure and internal consistency were evaluated. Relationships of demographic/clinical variables with total and domain-specific SWFC-Q scores were analyzed.ResultsInternal consistency was strong (Cronbach's Alpha = 0.925). Difficulty remembering names of famous people was the most frequently endorsed item (83%), whereas items related to the social impacts of SWFC were least frequently endorsed. Exploratory factor analysis revealed five distinct factors: General SWFC, SWFC-related errors and compensatory strategies, social and affective impacts of SWFC, proper noun retrieval difficulties, and common noun retrieval difficulties. Lower MMSE scores were associated with higher total SWFC. Older age was associated with higher total SWFC scores, greater general SWFC, greater proper and common noun retrieval difficulties. Female sex was associated with greater proper noun retrieval difficulties, and MCI status with greater social and affective impacts of SWFC.DiscussionIn aging, SWFC are a multidimensional rather than unitary construct. The novel SWFC-Q is a promising tool for characterizing the type and severity of specific SWFC and may facilitate future research into which complaint profiles are associated with adverse clinical outcomes, including Alzheimer's disease.

title: Inhibition of miR-199a-3p Enhances Neuronal Differentiation of Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Promotes Functional Recovery Following Spinal Cord Injury.
abstract: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) hold considerable promise for neural repair following spinal cord injury (SCI); however, their limited neuronal differentiation capacity remains a major translational barrier. MicroRNAs are critical regulators of stem cell fate, yet the specific miRNAs that constrain the neurogenic potential of BMSCs and the mechanisms through which they act remain incompletely defined. Comparative miRNA profiling of BMSCs, cortical neurons, and neural stem cells was performed using GeneChip microarray. The most differentially expressed miRNA, miR-199a-3p, was inhibited in BMSCs using a lentiviral sponge construct. Neuronal-like differentiation was evaluated by immunofluorescence and Western blot for beta-III tubulin, MAP-2, and mTOR. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in a rat T10-T11 contusion SCI model (n=20 per group) using the Basso-Beattie-Bresnahan (BBB) locomotor scale over 42 days. miR-199a-3p was the most significantly upregulated miRNA in BMSCs relative to neural cell populations. Sponge-mediated inhibition significantly reduced miR-199a-3p expression (p<0.01) and elevated mTOR protein levels. Anti-miR-199a-3p BMSCs expressed the neuronal markers beta-III tubulin and MAP-2 and adopted neurite-like morphological features in vitro. In the SCI model, transplantation of anti-miR-199a-3p BMSCs yielded significantly greater locomotor recovery (BBB score: 15.7+/-0.6) compared with empty vector-transduced BMSCs (13.0+/-0.8) and vehicle control groups (10.8+/-0.6) at six weeks post-injury (p<0.05). Selective inhibition of miR-199a-3p enhances the neurogenic potential of BMSCs, in part by derepressing mTOR, and significantly improves functional outcomes following SCI transplantation. Key words miR-199a-3p " Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells " Neuronal differentiation " mTOR " Spinal cord injury.

title: Artesunate Differentially Attenuates STZ-Induced Alzheimer-Like Pathology in Young and Old Mice by Targeting the Hippocampal Ferroptosis-Autophagy-Mitochondrial Redox Axis.
abstract: Aging is a critical determinant of Alzheimer disease (AD) susceptibility and therapeutic responsiveness. The current study aimed to evaluate the effect of artesunate on attenuating streptozotocin (STZ)-induced Alzheimer-like pathology by modulating the ferroptosis-autophagy-mitochondrial redox axis. STZ-induced AD-like pathology was established in young and old mice, which were divided into control, AD, and AD + artesunate groups. Cognitive function was measured with the Morris Water Maze (MWM) test to evaluate spatial learning and memory and using the novel object recognition (NOR) test to assess recognition memory. Protein expression levels of ferroptosis-related proteins (GPX4, SLC7A11, and ACSL4), autophagy proteins (LC3-I/II, Beclin-1, and p62), mitochondrial redox homeostasis and antioxidant defense proteins (SOD2 and HO-1), and synaptic integrity (PSD95 and synaptophysin) were evaluated. Artesunate significantly enhanced learning and memory in young AD mice, as evidenced by reduced escape latency and increased time spent in the target quadrant in the MWM, as well as a higher discrimination index in the NOR test. These behavioral improvements were associated with restored expression of GPX4 and SLC7A11 and suppression of ACSL4. These molecular changes were accompanied by a significant reduction in MDA and 4-HNE levels, enhanced autophagic flux (increased LC3-II/LC3-I ratio and Beclin-1 expression), and restoration of SOD2 and HO-1 levels. Moreover, artesunate reinstated synaptic integrity, as evidenced by increased expression of PSD95 and synaptophysin. Older AD mice showed slight cognitive recovery after artesunate administration, and exhibited poor performance in the MWM and NOR tests. Although targeting the ferroptosis-autophagy-mitochondrial redox axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy, aging significantly reduces molecular responsiveness and decreases treatment efficacy in AD. Key words Artesunate " Alzheimer disease " Ferroptosis " Autophagy " Mitochondrial redox.

title: Central GABAergic Modulation of Physostigmine-Induced Airway Constriction in Male Ferrets: A Bilateral Dorsal Motor Nucleus Microinjection Study.
abstract: The dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus (DMV) is a key brainstem structure involved in autonomic integration and vagal regulation of thoracic organs. This study examined whether localized GABA microinjection into the DMV modulates cholinergically induced airway mechanical responses in anesthetized male ferrets. Bilateral stereotaxic microinjections of GABA (10 mM; 50-70 nl) were performed in the DMV (AP -12.6 mm, ML 0 mm, DV -7.6 mm). Airway mechanics were evaluated by measuring tracheal segment pressure (Ptseg), lung resistance (RL), and dynamic compliance (Cdyn) at baseline, following intravenous physostigmine (100 microg/kg), and after GABA administration. Physostigmine significantly increased Ptseg and RL (P<0.01), indicating cholinergically mediated airway constriction. GABA microinjection attenuated these effects and significantly reduced Cdyn (P<0.05). Under controlled mechanical ventilation, these findings support a central inhibitory influence of DMV GABAergic signaling on vagally mediated airway responses during cholinergic activation. This study provides mechanistic proof-of-concept evidence for central modulation of airway mechanics and highlights the role of brainstem inhibitory circuits in autonomic respiratory regulation. Key words Dorsal vagal motor nucleus GABA microinjection " Physostigmine " Airway smooth muscle " Tracheal pressure " Cholinergic regulation.

title: ATP8B1-TMEM30B flippase activity maintains stereocilia lipid asymmetry required for hearing.
abstract: Sensory hair cells convert sound-induced vibrations into electrical signals through a process called mechano-electrical transduction (MET). While the protein components of the MET complex are well studied, increasing evidence indicates that MET channel properties are significantly modulated by the surrounding lipid bilayer. The asymmetric distribution of membrane lipids between the inner and outer membrane leaflets is well established to shape membrane mechanics. The recent discovery that the core MET components TMC1 and TMC2 also act as lipid scramblases suggests a direct role for membrane lipid asymmetry in the dynamic shaping of auditory transduction. Because scramblase activity of TMC1/2 disrupts lipid asymmetry, we hypothesized that an opposing flippase may be required to restore and maintain lipid asymmetry. Here, we identify the P4-ATPase ATP8B1 and its chaperone TMEM30B as selectively expressed in mouse outer hair cells (OHCs), enriched in stereocilia, and upregulated following the onset of MET and hearing. Loss of either protein results in elevated auditory brainstem response (ABR) thresholds, phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization, and rapid hair-cell degeneration, demonstrating that lipid homeostasis is crucial for OHC survival. Together, these findings establish ATP8B1 and TMEM30B as key regulators of membrane lipid asymmetry in sensory hair cells and establish TMEM30B as a novel deafness gene.

title: Racial/Ethnic Discrimination, E-Cigarette Use, and Parenting Among Black and Latina/o Adolescents: Sex Differences in Associations.
journal: Journal of studies on alcohol and drugs
abstract: Racial/ethnic discrimination is a chronic stressor associated with adolescent substance use. This study examined whether racial/ethnic discrimination was associated with e-cigarette use among Black and Latina/o adolescents and tested parenting factors, resistance to peer influence, sex (proxy for gender), and race/ethnicity as moderators. Data were drawn from 3,342 Black (41.7%) and Latina/o (58.3%) participants (48.7% female; mean age = 14.0, SD = 0.7) from Follow-up 4 of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study. Survey-weighted logistic regression analyses tested associations between discrimination and past-year e-cigarette use and moderation by parental monitoring, parental acceptance, resistance to peer influence, sex, and race/ethnicity. The association between discrimination and e-cigarette use was moderated by sex (p = .023). Discrimination was associated with e-cigarette use among males (OR = 1.70, 95% CI [1.32, 2.20]) but not among females (OR = 1.17, 95% CI [0.96, 1.42]). Parental monitoring (OR = 0.72, 95% CI [0.59, 0.89]) and parental acceptance (OR = 0.82, 95% CI [0.68, 0.99]) were independently associated with lower odds of e-cigarette use. Other tested moderators were nonsignificant. Findings identify discrimination as a potential intervention target for reducing e-cigarette use risk among Black and Latina/o adolescents and suggest positive parenting behaviors (i.e., monitoring, acceptance) may be broadly protective. Prevention efforts may benefit from addressing discrimination-related stress while supporting family-based protective processes.

title: Prevent cognitive decline in GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease using prasinezumab (PreCoDe): Rationale, design and cognitive endpoint for a proof-of-concept trial.
abstract: Cognitive decline represents a frequent and devastating complication of Parkinson's disease (PD) with no modifying treatments available so far. People with PD carrying a GBA1 mutation (PDGBA1) have a more severe course of the disease with rapid cognitive decline than idiopathic PD. Post-mortem and CSF biomarker studies support the hypothesis that this accelerated cognitive deterioration in PDGBA1 is primarily driven by a greater burden of cortical α-synuclein pathology. PDGBA1 show more extensive limbic and neocortical Lewy body pathology, while concomitant Alzheimer's pathology appears relatively limited. Similar findings have been reported in people with dementia with Lewy bodies carrying GBA1 mutations who represent a clinical and histopathological continuum to PD. We therefore hypothesize that treatment with prasinezumab, an α-synuclein-targeting antibody, could be effective in slowing cognitive decline in PDGBA1. We describe a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled proof-of-concept clinical trial to investigate if prasinezumab leads to a measurable delay of cognitive decline over a treatment duration of ∼2 years in PDGBA1 (PreCoDe; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07055087, EU-CT NUMBER 2024-513496-40-00). We introduce a new cognitive endpoint, the PD Cognitive Composite Score (PDCCS).

title: Self-Reported Procrastination as a Predictor of Students' Behavioral Delay and Academic Performance.
abstract: Educational research consistently shows that procrastination negatively affects students' achievement-related behaviors and contributes to academic maladjustment. Procrastination is typically linked to deficits in self-regulation and ineffective time management. This study examined whether individual differences in self-reported academic procrastination prospectively predict procrastination behavior across repeated academic activities and subsequent academic performance. Data from 245 undergraduates included self-reported procrastination (Academic Procrastination Scale-Short Form [APS-SF]), real-time delays in submitting three academic quizzes, self-reported exam-preparation timing, and academic performance. APS-SF scores significantly predicted both real-time procrastination and final examination marks, indicating that individual differences in self-reported procrastination are prospectively associated with subsequent patterns of academic delay and performance. Moreover, exam-preparation timing partially mediated the association between APS-SF scores and final examination performance, with higher self-reported procrastination being associated with later initiation of exam preparation, which in turn was associated with lower examination marks. The findings provide evidence that delayed engagement with academic demands may partly account for the association between self-reported procrastination and poorer academic performance, while also supporting the usefulness of self-report measures as indicators of subsequent procrastination-related behavior.

title: From Sight-Reading to Practiced Performance: Characterizing Upper-Body Kinematics in Expert Pianists Using Markerless Motion Capture.
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
abstract: Sight-reading on the piano demands rapid spatiotemporal adjustments in movement patterns, yet its biomechanical basis and immediate practice effects remain underexplored. We characterized upper-body kinematics in expert pianists across two ecologically related performance states: initial sight-reading of unfamiliar musical material and performance of the same material following brief practice/familiarization. Twenty expert pianists performed two excerpts: a rapid scale-like (dexterous) task and a repetitive chordal task, followed by up to 10 min of practice. Movements were recorded at 120 Hz using eight cameras and a markerless motion capture system (Theia3D), yielding shoulder-, elbow-, and wrist-angle trajectories. The number of direction changes, a position-domain measure of trajectory reversals, was the primary outcome; range of motion (ROM) and median angular velocity were secondary outcomes. Short practice was associated with fewer direction changes in selected upper-body joint-angle trajectories in both tasks, with more widespread changes in the chordal task. No significant practice-related changes in ROM or median angular velocity were observed after correcting for multiple comparisons. These findings demonstrate measurable short-term changes in upper-body joint-angle trajectories between initial sight-reading and performance following brief practice and illustrate the application of markerless motion capture to the study of ecologically relevant, unconstrained piano performance.

title: Disease Burden and Direct Health-Care Spending on Brain Conditions in Switzerland: Findings from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 Study for the Implementation of the Swiss Brain Health Plan.
journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists

title: Automated Home-Cage Sipper Devices Reveal Age and Sex Differences in Ethanol Consumption Patterns.
abstract: Alcohol consumption and alcohol use disorder (AUD) are influenced by circadian rhythms, which differ with age and sex. Little research has compared circadian ethanol consumption patterns across ages and sexes. Cost-effective, open-source Arduino-based home-cage sipper devices could elucidate these patterns. We hypothesized these devices would reveal phase and/or amplitude changes in circadian drinking rhythms in ethanol-drinking mice that would vary by age and sex. We used Arduino-based home-cage sipper devices in continuous-access two-bottle choice (2 bc) with water and ethanol (10% v/v) for 14 days to measure drinking patterns of male and female adolescent (3-week), young adult (6-week), and mature adult (18-week) C57BL/6J mice. Grams per kilogram (g/kg) fluid consumption was manually recorded at the beginning of each dark cycle, while sipper devices continuously recorded drinking. Manually collected 2 bc data confirmed greater ethanol consumption in females and stepwise decreases in total fluid consumption with age in ethanol-drinking females and in both sexes in the water-only groups. Correlations of manually recorded versus sipper count data were strong and significant for ethanol, but weaker for water. Blood ethanol concentrations significantly correlated with sipper data, indicating sipper devices can determine temporal ethanol consumption. Sipper devices uncovered subtle differences in circadian rhythms by age, group, and ethanol consumption, including minor phase advancement with ethanol consumption with age in females, but delay in males, as well as a female-specific phase delay and weaker amplitude in total fluid consumption across age groups with ethanol consumption. We show these devices capture circadian patterns of drinking behavior differing by age, sex, and ethanol consumption inaccessible by manual 2 bc measurements. Future studies may examine older age groups and further dissect circadian drinking patterns by age and sex and their molecular mechanisms relevant to AUD pathogenesis.

title: Attribution Gates Self-Belief Updating From Social Feedback.
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
abstract: Social feedback can shape self-beliefs, yet its informational value is often uncertain because it depends on others' motives and accuracy. We tested how people evaluate the credibility of social feedback and how these credibility-related attributional judgments regulate self-belief updating as a function of feedback valence and expectancy congruence. Participants interacted in small groups and subsequently received anonymous feedback on self-relevant traits. Participants were informed that some feedback might have been manipulated. In fact, the experimenter manipulated the feedback to be positive, neutral, or negative relative to initial self-beliefs. Negative feedback and expectancy-incongruent feedback were more likely to be attributed externally (i.e., judged manipulated). Belief updating critically depended on these credibility judgments: when feedback was judged genuine, self-beliefs updated in a graded, valence-consistent manner from negative to neutral to positive feedback; when feedback was judged manipulated, this valence-dependent updating collapsed and updating was driven primarily by expectations. A three-way interaction further showed that belief updating reflected the combined influence of expected feedback valence, received feedback valence, and credibility attributions. These findings support a two-stage account in which credibility assessments gate whether social information is treated as reliable evidence, with implications for how biased credibility judgments may foster maladaptive self-beliefs relevant to psychopathology.

title: Donor identity in Aotearoa New Zealand: early contact between parents and identity-release clinic donors, same-donor siblings and donors' raised children.
abstract: Contact among donor-conceived people (DCP), families and donors is increasing, but little is known about contact before DCP reach adulthood. Although DCP in New Zealand can access donor identifying information at 18, parents may request information earlier, enabling 'early' contact. This study reports findings from the Donor Identity Aotearoa New Zealand survey examining contact between 189 parents of DCP aged 7-18 and clinic-recruited donors, same-donor siblings, and donors' raised children. Quantitative data were analysed using Stata 17BE and qualitative responses were analysed thematically. Eighty-six parents (45.5%) had accessed donor identifying information, 42 (22.2%) had met the donor and 34 (18.0%) reported other contact. Among the 91 parents aware of same-donor siblings, 14 (15.4%) had met their parents; 16 (17.6%) had met a sibling. Twenty-two of 107 (20.8%) parents aware of donors' children had met them. Contact did not differ by family type, donation type, or child age. Qualitative findings suggested positive experiences, alongside parents' negotiation of donor-related families' roles, often with limited guidance. Forty-six parents (24.3%) wanted help with contact; 42 (22.2%) were unsure, and 7/57 (12.1%) already in contact wanted additional assistance. Findings indicate parents may benefit from support to initiate and maintain early contact in New Zealand.

title: Synaptic Plasticity Deficits via Aberrant Engagement of Metaplasticity in the Hippocampus of PS19 Mice.
abstract: Tauopathy is characterized by progressive synaptic failure and neuroinflammation, yet the laminar-specific nature of these disruptions remains poorly understood. We investigated hippocampal functional integrity and glial reactivity in 8-10-month-old PS19 (P301S) mice, a period of advanced tau pathology. Electrophysiological recordings in the CA1 stratum radiatum revealed an unexpected increase in field EPSP input/output curves despite profound deficits in both early and maintenance phases of LTP. Conversely, the dentate gyrus exhibited reduced field EPSP input/output curves and impaired LTP maintenance, alongside significant paired-pulse plasticity changes not observed in CA1. Furthermore, we demonstrate that trans-regional metaplasticity, as driven by prior activity in the stratum oriens (SO) in a way that inhibits subsequent LTP in wild-type mice, is occluded in PS19 mice. These data suggest that the tauopathy hippocampus exists in a "metaplastic" state, inhibiting future LTP. Immunofluorescence studies revealed that while astrogliosis and microglial activation were pan-hippocampal, specific neuroinflammatory markers exhibited striking laminar specificity. The neuroinflammatory astrocyte marker C3 mean intensity was significantly upregulated only in the SO, and the lysosomal marker CD68 showed heightened occupancy specifically in the SO and stratum lacunosum-moleculare. Our findings indicate that tau pathology does not affect the hippocampus uniformly. Instead, it induces region-specific shifts in synaptic efficacy and a breakdown of metaplastic control that coincides with anatomically localized neuroinflammatory signaling.

title: A Multi-Modal Posterior Network for Memory Retrieval From Visuospatial and Olfactory Context.
abstract: Retrieval of context-dependent episodic memories is thought to rely on a temporo-parietal network comprising hippocampal, parahippocampal, retrosplenial, and posterior parietal cortices. However, although real experiences occur within rich multi-modal contexts, and computational models emphasize convergence zones and the need for cross-modal binding, experimental evidence from humans predominantly relies on a single contextual modality (often visual). Thus the specific functional contributions of the identified brain regions to unimodal or multimodal retrieval remain unclear. Here, we analyzed a dataset from 2003 using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and multi-modal virtual reality to compare activity during retrieval of newly formed events from visuo-spatial or olfactory contexts. Contextual retrieval of either kind engaged left posterior hippocampal, anterior thalamic, retrosplenial, and medial and left posterior parietal cortices, consistent with cross-modal processing. By contrast, right parahippocampal and right posterior parietal activity specifically reflected retrieval via visuo-spatial context, and insula and cingulate gyrus activity retrieval via olfactory context. Our data identify the subcomponents of the temporo-parietal network involved in contextual retrieval from multiple modalities on the one hand, while highlighting the subcomponents that are specific to visuospatial contextual retrieval on the other hand.

title: Multi-Echo Versus T2-Prepared pCASL: Methodological Considerations for Measuring Water Transport Across the Blood-Brain Barrier.
abstract: T2-based pCASL measures water transport across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) by separating signal from intravascular and extravascular label based on the distinct T2 relaxation times of blood and tissue. Two commonly used approaches encode T2 information differently: Multi-echo sequences employ a multi-echo turbo spin-echo readout, whereas T2-prepared (T2-prep) sequences apply a preparation module consisting of multiple 180° refocusing pulses prior to a single-echo readout. It remains unclear which approach provides more reliable estimates of BBB water exchange. This study directly compares them in terms of T2 estimation and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). In vivo experiments implemented each method separately, as well as in a single combined sequence, using Hadamard-encoded multi-post-labeling delay (PLDs = 600,1600, 2600 ms) pCASL. Simulations evaluated the effects of T2 decay and label arrival during the readout. T2 estimates were comparable at PLDs of 1600 and 2600 ms. At the shortest PLD of 600 ms, multi-echo yielded lower T2. Multi-echo demonstrated higher temporal and spatial SNR, whereas T2-prep showed increased T2 blurring and image artifacts in the unsubtracted images, consistent with simulations. Although multi-echo provides superior SNR, it may underestimate T2 at short PLDs. The underlying cause of this finding remains unresolved; however, preliminary simulations indicate it could result from partial signal crushing of flowing spins by readout gradients. In contrast, the longer readout of the T2-prep approach is more prone to blurring and artifacts. These findings highlight important trade-offs between the two techniques and underscore the need for careful sequence selection in T2-based BBB water exchange studies.

title: Gallic acid ameliorates depressive-like behaviour associated with type-2 diabetes mellitus by mitigating oxidative stress.
abstract: Diabetes is linked with depression due to insulin resistance. Gallic acid, a natural polyphenol, has been demonstrated to have benefits against experimental hyperglycemia. In the present study, we investigated the antidepressant effect of gallic acid on depression-like behaviour in hyperglycaemic rats. Hyperglycemia was induced in rats using dexamethasone (2 mg/kg i.p.) for 7 days, followed by exposure to chronic unpredictable mild stressors to produce depression-like phenotypes. Animals were subjected to daily oral administration for 21 days. Behavioural paradigms like the sucrose preference test, forced swim test, locomotor activity, novelty-suppressed feeding, and novel object recognition were performed. Biochemical estimations, including glucose levels, oxidative stress parameters, and neurotransmitter levels, were performed. The findings indicated that administration of gallic acid attenuated depressive-like behaviour. Furthermore, treatment with gallic acid also demonstrated better cognitive ability and amelioration of behavioural abnormalities. Gallic acid treatment normalized the elevated blood glucose in diabetic rats. A significant improvement in antioxidant parameters was noticed after treatment with gallic acid. Additionally, altered levels of neurotransmitters like serotonin and dopamine were also improved by gallic acid treatment. Histopathological evaluation of the brain demonstrated increased neural density and restoration of normal neural morphology. Gallic acid may ameliorate depression associated with hyperglycemia by mitigating oxidative stress and neurological dysfunction in the brain. Therefore, the current study provides evidence that gallic acid may exert antidepressant-like effects in the experimental model of hyperglycemia and depression.

title: Synthesis of O-Propargylated Chalcones as Multitarget Inhibitors of Diabetes- and Alzheimer's Disease-Related Enzymes: Biological Evaluation and Molecular Insights.
abstract: A series of 4-O-propargylated chalcones (4a-l) was synthesized via Claisen-Schmidt condensation using the hydroxide-functionalized ionic liquid [BMIM]OH as a green and efficient catalytic system under mild conditions. The developed methodology afforded excellent yields (89%-95%) within short reaction times (15-25 min.), surpassing conventional and ultrasound-assisted approaches. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their multifunctional biological activities against α-amylase, α-glucosidase, AChE, and BChE. Compound 4b (R = 4-NO2) displayed potent α-amylase inhibition (IC50 = 6.54 μM), whereas 4c (R = 3-NO2) exhibited excellent α-glucosidase inhibition (IC50 = 6.75 μM), comparable to acarbose. In cholinesterase assays, 4l (R = 4-NMe2) emerged as a highly potent dual AChE/BChE inhibitor with IC50 values of 0.06 and 0.03 μM, respectively. Selected derivatives also demonstrated significant antioxidant and anti-glycation activities together with low cytotoxicity toward WI-38 cells. Molecular docking and 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable binding interactions within the enzyme active sites. DFT calculations revealed that HOMO-LUMO energy gaps, charge delocalization, and electrostatic potential distributions strongly influenced biological activity. ADMET predictions further supported favorable drug-likeness and oral bioavailability. Overall, O-propargylated chalcones represent promising multifunctional scaffolds for developing dual antidiabetic and anti-Alzheimer agents.

title: AAV-mediated neurogenetic therapy for Huntington's disease: from experimental hope to responsible clinical translation.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which no disease-modifying therapy currently exists. Gene therapy using adeno-associated virus (AAV) has become a potential experimental intervention for the molecular etiology of mutant huntingtin (mHTT). This review is a critical analysis of the present state of AAV-based therapeutic interventions that may be considered through the lens of translational preparedness instead of early clinical efficacy. Relevant literature was searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published from January 2020 to June 2026, using keywords related to Huntington's disease, AAV gene therapy, gene silencing, genome editing, safety, and clinical translation. The essential factors are the design of vectors, delivery methods, the mechanistic differences between gene silencing and editing, and safety issues raised due to preliminary clinical trials. The issues of ethical, regulatory, and health-system preparedness, which include neurosurgical risks, patient selection, long-term monitoring, and regulatory divergence between the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency (EMA) and Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), are assessed in terms of their influence on clinical scalability. We emphasize on the unbridgeable disconnect between the experimental promise and the true applicability by combining trial evidence with regulatory and implementation understanding. Long-term sustainability of AAV therapies will depend on decade-long safety surveillance, transparent governance, and coordinated health-system readiness.

title: White Matter Geometric Disorganization Links Subcortical Degeneration to Motor Impairment in Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3.
abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3) is the most common hereditary ataxia caused by CAG repeat expansion in the ATXN3 gene. However, the structural mechanisms linking genetic burden, neurodegeneration, and motor impairment remain poorly understood. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 105 genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 133 healthy controls. Diffusion MRI and structural MRI were acquired using harmonized protocols and harmonized across sites using ComBat. Director field analysis (DFA) was used to quantify WM geometric organization (splay, bend, and twist). Voxel-wise, region-of-interest, correlation, and mediation analyses were performed to examine associations among WM geometry, subcortical atrophy, CAG repeat length, and motor impairment measured by the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA). SCA3 patients exhibited widespread increases in splay and bend together with reductions in twist across cerebellar peduncles, projection, commissural, and association fibers. Geometric abnormalities were substantially more extensive than alterations detected by conventional diffusion metrics. Significant atrophy was observed predominantly in the cerebellar white matter, brainstem, putamen, globus pallidus, thalamus, and caudate. Longer CAG repeat expansions were associated with greater geometric disruption within motor-related pathways. Furthermore, geometric abnormalities within the external capsule and superior cerebellar peduncle partially mediated the association between basal ganglia atrophy and motor impairment. White matter geometric alterations may represent a potential imaging phenotype linking genetic burden, subcortical neurodegeneration, and motor disability in SCA3. These findings provide new insights into the network mechanisms underlying disease progression and highlight WM geometric metrics as potential imaging biomarkers for SCA3.

title: Global reporting of Brugada syndrome in VigiBase®: A disproportionality analysis.
abstract: Brugada syndrome (BrS) represents a rare but potentially malignant cardiac channelopathy, which may be precipitated by drugs, although data mainly derive from case reports/series. To describe the global reporting of BrS with drugs, including co-occurrence patterns, and identify novel potential associations. We used VigiBase® to perform descriptive and disproportionality analyses. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian information component (IC) with relevant 95% confidence/credibility intervals (95% CI) were used as disproportionality measures to identify signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR). We performed a network analysis to assess the co-occurrence patterns of related medications based on Jaccard similarity. We included 544 deduplicated cases of BrS (94.7% serious events, 30.9% females, median time to onset of 30 days, 40.8% physician-reported, 63% from North America), with bupropion (n = 50), nortriptyline (n = 40) and flecainide (n = 34) as most frequently reported suspected drugs. Among 39 drugs with at least four reports, 32 emerged with an SDR, of which 17 were not listed in the BrS website (http://www.brugadadrugs.org), such as clozapine and loperamide (often overdosed). The co-occurrence network included 17 medications, regardless of the labelled role (suspected, interacting or concomitant), with a total of 12 potential co-occurrences; fentanyl exhibited the highest closeness centrality (1.0), whereas the strongest co-occurrence was reported between bupropion and nortriptyline (Jaccard similarity of 0.31). Notwithstanding limitations related to pharmacovigilance and the complex BrS pathophysiology, we identified 32 medications with over-reporting of BrS, including 17 drugs not listed in the BrS website as well as clusters in affective disorders and anaesthesia.

title: Exploring How Home Care Workers Build Trust and Perceive Their Competence in Dementia Care: A Swedish Qualitative Study.
abstract: Home care workers (HCWs') play a central role in supporting older adults with dementia who live at home. Despite the frequent association between high-quality home care and person-centred approaches, there is limited clarity on how such care should be defined and practiced from the perspective of HCWs'. This study explores how HCWs' understand high-quality care for older adults with dementia and how they work to achieve it in daily practice. We conducted three focus group discussions with a total of 21 HCWs' from different agencies in Stockholm, Sweden, between November and December 2024. Transcripts were analysed using an inductive thematic analysis. The analysis generated one overarching theme: Quality of care is achieved through trustful relationships in combination with professional competence. This theme is supported by three interrelated sub-themes; (a) Conveying a positive feeling: Communicating calmness and reassurance, (b) Walking a fine line: Balancing safety, autonomy and dignity and (c) Holistic Competence: Combining education, experience and personal attributes. High-quality dementia home care relies on the integration of professional competence and relationship-based trust. Ensuring continuity, flexibility to meet individual needs, interprofessional collaboration and ongoing professional development are key organizational prerequisites for delivering person-centred care and supporting older adults to live well at home.

title: Cerebral microvascular vasospasm after stroke and cardiac arrest: mechanisms of no-reflow and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Acute ischaemic stroke and resuscitation after cardiac arrest are often accompanied by persistent cerebral microvascular dysfunction, known as the no-reflow phenomenon, which may contribute to secondary brain injury despite successful macrovascular reperfusion. Although no-reflow is a multifactorial process, microvascular vasospasm may represent a central and potentially modifiable component of the broader microvascular response. Increasing evidence from preclinical studies indicates that microvascular vasospasm arises from a complex interplay between neuronal, glial, endothelial, and mural cell signalling within the neurovascular unit. Key mechanisms include peri-infarct and anoxic spreading depolarisations, endothelin-1- and 20-HETE-mediated vasoconstrictor signalling, and Ca2+ overload in vascular smooth muscle cells and low-order capillary ensheathing pericytes, which together promote sustained vasocontraction and impaired capillary perfusion. In addition, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and inflammatory processes further exacerbate microvascular dysregulation during ischaemia-reperfusion, potentially impairing glymphatic transport. Experimental imaging studies demonstrate that these mechanisms evolve dynamically over time. While the onset of microvascular vasoconstriction may be similar after stroke and cardiac arrest, the underlying mechanisms driving these changes can differ between these conditions.
