This review summarises current knowledge of the mechanisms underlying cerebral microvascular vasospasm following cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion and discusses potential therapeutic targets aimed at preventing spreading depolarisation and relaxing vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes to restore microcirculatory flow after hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury.

title: Multimodal Treatment and Sustained Rehabilitation in Primary CNS Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma: A Five-Year Survivor With Long-Term Remission.
abstract: Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is an aggressive extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma confined to the central nervous system and is most commonly associated with immunosuppression, although it may also occur in immunocompetent individuals. We report a case of a 51-year-old immunocompetent female who presented with a two-week history of slurred speech and right-sided facial weakness, initially managed as Bell's palsy. Neuroimaging revealed a solitary left parietal lesion. She underwent craniotomy, and histopathological examination confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma. The postoperative course was complicated within 24 hours by intracranial haemorrhage requiring re-exploration, followed by multifocal ischaemic infarcts. Subsequently, she received high-dose methotrexate-based chemotherapy with rituximab, followed by whole-brain radiotherapy. Over the ensuing months, the patient demonstrated gradual neurological improvement with rehabilitation. At five-year follow-up, she remains in remission with stable neurological status. This case highlights the occurrence of PCNSL in an immunocompetent patient, the potential for severe treatment-related complications, and the possibility of meaningful neurological recovery following sequential oncologic and haemorrhagic brain injury.

title: From Biomimicry to Engineering: Membrane-Based Nanomedicine for Central Nervous System Therapy.
abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) disorders remain difficult to treat because therapeutic agents must reach disease-relevant tissues and cells at an appropriate exposure. For systemically administered therapies, this often requires avoiding rapid clearance and crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Membrane-based nanomedicine, including cell membrane-coated nanoparticles and extracellular vesicles (EVs), offers biological interfaces with source-dependent properties that can be selected and engineered for specific delivery requirements. This review organizes engineering strategies into three non-exclusive categories: source-cell engineering, including phenotype modulation and genetic programming; membrane hybridization, which combines membrane interfaces; and surface functionalization, which introduces additional ligands or functional components. These approaches can be combined within a single formulation. Drawing on models of neurodegenerative disease, ischemic injury, brain tumors, spinal cord injury, and selected psychiatric conditions, we compare the intended functions of these operations, the experimental evidence supporting their contributions, and the associated therapeutic outcomes. Particular attention is given to disease context, administration route, and comparator design. We also discuss membrane source standardization, scalable manufacturing, safety, and the limitations of current preclinical models. This perspective connects membrane design with defined CNS delivery requirements and the evidence needed to assess functional benefit and translational feasibility.

title: HSPiP-QbD Enabled Optimized Tolterodine Lipid Nanoparticles with GastroPlus-Based in vivo Prediction and in vivo Studies for Controlled Drug Delivery.
abstract: This study optimized tolterodine tartrate loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (TOTA-SLNs) for sustained delivery and improved oral bioavailability, with GastroPlus-enabled predictive human regional absorption. The HSPiP software predicted suitable excipients based on theoretical solubility and Hansen solubility parameters (HSP). The solubility data and Taguchi model (identified prime factors) set a range of compritol 888 ATO (CATO as factor X1) and stirring rate (as factor X2) in QbD-enabled optimization for the particle size, %EE (percent entrapment efficiency), and total drug content. A central composite design was implemented considering particle size (Y1), %EE (Y2), and total drug content (Y3) as responses. The optimized TOTA-SLN6 was characterized for size, zeta potential (ZP), polydispersity index (PDI), and morphology. In vitro drug release behavior was compared against the drug suspension (TOTA-SUS) in phosphate buffer solution (pH 7.4). An in vitro hemolysis study ensured minimum erythrocytes interaction as a preliminary safety indicator. In vivo rat data was used to predict human regional absorption in humans using GastroPlus simulation. The HSPiP and the Taguchi model predicted suitable excipients and identified CATO and stirring rate as main factors, respectively. CCD-enabled an optimized TOTA-SLN6 with desired formulation characteristics (size ~ 216 nm, ZP ~ -22 mV, PDI ~ 0.3, %EE ~ 87, and TDC ~ 97%). Spherical TOTA-SLN6 showed sustained drug release (98.44% over 24 h) and hemocompatibility (<20% hemolysis over the explored concentrations) with rat erythrocytes. Improved pharmacokinetic data ensured that SLNs improved oral bioavailability in rats and high in vivo absorption in humans as evidenced with GastroPlus based predictive data.

title: Spiritual Health and Psychological Well-Being and Their Relationship with General Self-Efficacy in Mothers of Children with Intellectual Disability and Autism Spectrum Disorders.
abstract: Objective: Mothers of children suffering with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID) experience substantial psychological challenges that may affect their perceived self-efficacy. While psychological well-being and spiritual health are considered important protective factors, their relative contributions to general self-efficacy in this population remain insufficiently explored in Iran. This study aimed to investigate whether psychological well-being and spiritual health are correlated with the general self-efficacy of mothers of children with ID or ASD in Qom, Iran. Method : This was a correlational cross-sectional study involving the participation of 100 mothers of children with ID (n = 49) and ASD (n = 51) who were enrolled via multi-stage cluster sampling method. The participants completed the Spiritual Health Questionnaire for the Iranian Population, the Ryff Psychological Well-Being Questionnaire, and the Sherer Self-Efficacy Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficients and stepwise multiple regression analysis in SPSS version 22, with the significance level set at P 0.05). Regression analyses showed that psychological well-being explained 38% of the variance in general self-efficacy among mothers of children with ASD and 42% among mothers of children with ID (P < 0.001). Conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of psychological well-being as a substantial predictor of general self-efficacy among mothers of children with ID and ASD. Thus, interventions to strengthen maternal self-efficacy are recommended to be considered a means of promoting self-efficacy, while the role of spiritual health requires further study.

title: ATLAS-FREE FUNCTIONAL BRAIN CONNECTOME ANALYSIS VIA TASK-DRIVEN PARCELLATION.
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
abstract: Functional brain connectome analysis models brain connectivity as a network, where nodes represent brain regions and edges capture their functional interactions. Existing methods mainly rely on predefined atlases (e.g., AAL) to partition the brain and extract regional signals. However, these predefined atlases lack task specificity and cannot capture individual variability, limiting their effectiveness in clinical prediction. To address these challenges, we propose AFCON, an atlas-free framework that jointly optimizes brain parcellation and connectome analysis in a task-driven manner. AFCON adaptively generates individualized, task-specific parcellations directly from fMRI data, ensuring better alignment with downstream predictions and offering enhanced interpretability. Moreover, we introduce two neurobiologically informed regularizers to ensure plausible parcellations: a spatial compactness regularizer to promote anatomical coherence, and a balanced distribution regularizer to mitigate extreme parcel size imbalances. Experiments on ADHD and ADNI datasets show that AFCON achieves robust predictions, and importantly, identifies disease-relevant brain regions that reveal disrupted functional connections, improving both interpretability and clinical relevance. The code is available at https://github.com/LearningKeqi/AFCON.

title: Beyond decibels alone: environmental noise, auditory diversity, and person-environment interactions in autism.
abstract: Environmental noise is a ubiquitous physical exposure and a biologically active non-auditory stressor, yet its relevance to autism has received substantially less attention compared to chemical components of the urban exposome. Two questions are often conflated: whether prenatal or early-life noise contributes to autism-related neurodevelopmental susceptibility and whether adverse auditory environments increase functional burden after autistic characteristics are present. In this structured narrative review, we integrate environmental epidemiology, developmental and auditory neuroscience, sleep and stress research, and environmental acoustics within a two-pathway life-course framework. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception through 4 September 2026, supplemented by targeted Google Scholar searching. We included English-language peer-reviewed primary studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and authoritative guidance or standards documents and excluded conference abstracts, dissertations, and preprints. Evidence was prioritized by directness to the autism question, study design, exposure characterization, outcome validity, precision, and recency; the evidence matrix is intentionally selective. Direct human evidence that quantified environmental noise independently increasing the risk of autism diagnosis or persistently worsening autistic traits is sparse and inconsistent, and current data do not support a causal claim. A more direct functional evidence stream-studies conducted on autistic participants that experimentally manipulate auditory conditions and/or measure real-world functional outcomes-indicates that some autistic individuals show altered auditory responsivity, reduced or delayed habituation, speech-in-noise and selective-attention difficulties, and greater burden in noisy or unpredictable settings. We conceptualize this pathway as a person-environment interaction in which acoustic structure, sensory phenotype, task demand, and predictability or control jointly shape functioning. Standard metrics such as LAeq, Lden, and Lnight remain necessary for comparability and policy and are supplemented, not replaced, by multidimensional characterization. Event peaks and temporal fluctuation receive empirical support from studies on child neurodevelopment, whereas spectral content, reverberation, source multiplicity, predictability, controllability, and personal time-activity patterns remain framework-generated hypotheses requiring direct autism-specific testing. This framework separates etiologic inference from phenotypic modification and identifies testable priorities for early-life research and co-designed acoustic accessibility.

title: When Artificial Intelligence Becomes Irreplaceable: A Proposed Framework for AI Attachment Dysregulation.
abstract: People may experience emotionally meaningful bonds with artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Attachment and distress after a companion changes or disappears are increasingly measurable, but neither establishes psychopathology. This editorial proposes AI attachment dysregulation as a research framework for repeated difficulty adjusting engagement with a particular perceived AI relationship, accompanied by persistent, clinically significant distress or functional impairment. Its proposed contribution is to distinguish reliance on relational continuity from dependence on AI capabilities generally. Assessment should separate attachment strength, regulatory flexibility, and independently measured consequences, while accounting for practical dependence, limited access to other support, and established psychiatric conditions. The proposed model examines how relational expectations, emotional relief, and flexibility in adapting engagement may shape whether these bonds support or interfere with daily life. Prospective studies should test whether attachment-related inflexibility predicts later difficulties beyond existing dependency measures and whether the construct improves assessment or intervention. Strong attachment may coexist with autonomy and benefit. The framework is intended to support testable research and proportionate clinical inquiry; it does not establish a diagnosis, neural mechanism, or validated treatment.

title: Cortical spreading depression on Riemannian 2-manifolds: eikonal-curvature analysis and sulcal trapping.
abstract: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is a slowly propagating wave of near-complete neuronal depolarization underlying migraine aura and implicated in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Existing reaction-diffusion models of CSD treat the cortex as a flat Euclidean domain, ignoring its highly folded, individually variable geometry. We develop a fully covariant FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) reaction-diffusion system on a smooth compact Riemannian 2-manifold [Formula: see text] representing the cortical sheet, in which the Euclidean Laplacian is replaced by the Laplace-Beltrami operator [Formula: see text]. Three mathematical results are established: (i) local and global well-posedness in [Formula: see text] together with positive invariance of the physiological region via parabolic semigroup theory; (ii) a curvature-corrected eikonal relation [Formula: see text], in which the wavefront speed is modulated by the geodesic curvature of the front; and (iii) a sulcal-trapping theorem giving an explicit criterion under which an excitable wave entering a sulcus (negative Gauss curvature region) remains confined to it. Numerically, we develop two complementary solvers: a discrete exterior calculus (DEC) scheme on triangulated surfaces using the cotangent Laplacian with implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate that evaluates [Formula: see text] via the closest-point projection of the ambient Euclidean Laplacian. The PINN framework supports both forward simulation and the inverse identification of excitability fields from sparse observations, and a noise-ablation study quantifies its practical identifiability. The parameters of the slow subsystem and of the coupling functions are inherited from our published, cohort-calibrated thalamocortical model, which was calibrated against 67 paired-pulse somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings from nine analysable animals of a cohort of 14 male Wistar rats (1, 233 sweeps) acquired in the Neuroscience Laboratory of Gazi University, with CSD induced by topical KCl application. We validate convergence on [Formula: see text] with the spectral ground-truth [Formula: see text], exhibit a propagating ring wave with a refractory tail, and verify the eikonal-curvature prediction across two orders of magnitude in geodesic curvature, including the leading correction due to the recovery variable; a mesh-convergence study yields explicit resolution requirements for evaluating the trapping criterion on MRI-derived cortical surfaces.

title: Pathophysiology of slow-transit constipation: from cellular mechanisms to personalized therapy.
abstract: Slow-transit constipation (STC) represents a severe and often refractory subtype of chronic constipation, defined by markedly prolonged colonic transit and a poor response to standard therapies. It is estimated to affect ∼15%-30% of patients with chronic constipation. Despite extensive investigation, its underlying pathogenesis has yet to be fully elucidated. In this review, we synthesized recent advances in the multidimensional pathophysiology of STC, encompassing dysfunction of the enteric and autonomic nervous systems, injury to interstitial cells of Cajal and smooth muscle, imbalances in neurotransmitter and hormonal signaling, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and low-grade inflammation, with an emphasis on how these factors interact to generate substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. Given the limited and often variable efficacy of existing treatments, there is an urgent need for mechanism-based, precision-targeted therapies. Emerging approaches, including neuromodulation, regenerative cell-based therapies, and microbiome modulation, have shown encouraging signals, although their efficacy and safety require confirmation in larger, well-designed clinical trials. Future research should integrate molecular omics with clinical phenotyping to stratify patients with STC and identify robust biomarkers, thereby guiding personalized interventions. Continued translational efforts are expected to bridge molecular insights with clinical practice, laying the groundwork for precise and durable therapies that ultimately improve outcomes and quality of life for individuals with STC.

title: Emerging Nanomaterials: A Promise to Overcome Temozolomide Resistance in Glioma.
abstract: Gliomas represent the most prevalent primary malignant brain tumors in adults, characterized by poor prognoses despite advancements in multimodal therapies. Temozolomide (TMZ) remains a fundamental component of glioma chemotherapy; however, its clinical effectiveness is often compromised by both intrinsic and acquired resistance. This review adopts a mechanism-guided framework to integrate key resistance determinants, such as O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase-mediated DNA repair, mismatch repair deficiency, alternative DNA damage repair pathways, autophagy-associated survival mechanisms, and protective influences from the tumor microenvironment. Utilizing this framework, we critically assess nanomaterial-based strategies designed to address specific resistance mechanisms, including targeted TMZ delivery, co-delivery of resistance-modulating agents, microenvironment-responsive drug release, and multifunctional therapeutic platforms. Emphasis is placed on comparing their mechanistic rationale, therapeutic benefits, limitations, toxicity concerns, and levels of supporting evidence, rather than merely cataloguing previously reported nanomaterial systems. Although nanomaterials hold significant promise for enhancing blood-brain barrier penetration, tumor selectivity, drug accumulation, and combination therapy, substantial challenges persist, including biological heterogeneity, complex pharmacokinetics, long-term safety, reproducibility, and clinical translation. By directly correlating the defined mechanisms of TMZ resistance with corresponding nanomaterial interventions and critically evaluating the robustness of current evidence, this review offers a structured framework for the rational development and future translation of nanomaterial-based strategies for TMZ-resistant gliomas.

title: Patent Foramen Ovale Closure Outcomes in Patients of Advanced Age (PFO-COPA): Protocol for a Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is a common cardiac abnormality associated with paradoxical embolism and ischemic stroke. Randomized trials have demonstrated the benefit of percutaneous PFO closure in patients aged <60 years with cryptogenic stroke, but nearly all trials have excluded individuals aged ≥60 years, leaving a critical evidence gap in older populations, in whom competing stroke mechanisms are prevalent. There is currently no dedicated, validated framework to guide closure decisions in this age group. Consequently, clinical practice remains highly variable, and closure decisions are made based on extrapolation from younger cohorts rather than robust evidence. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of PFO closure compared with medical therapy in patients aged ≥60 years with cryptogenic stroke and a confirmed PFO. This multicenter international retrospective cohort study will include consecutive patients aged ≥60 years with imaging-confirmed ischemic stroke, a confirmed PFO, and no alternative definite etiology of stroke after standard diagnostic evaluation, who underwent either percutaneous PFO closure or medical therapy between 2015 and 2025. Outcomes will be collected through standardized chart review and entered into a centralized REDCap database. The primary outcome will be the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke. Secondary outcomes will include major bleeding, new-onset atrial fibrillation, device-related complications, and mortality. Time-to-event analyses, Cox regression, and propensity score methods will be used to adjust for confounding. As of October 2026, 51 centers from 10 countries (Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Greece, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Portugal, Spain, and the United States) have formally agreed to participate in the study. Each site is currently in the process of securing institutional review board (IRB) approval and executing data use agreements. A standardized variable dictionary has been distributed to all centers to ensure consistency in data collection. As of October 2026, 45 centers have applied for local IRB approval, 5 centers have obtained IRB approval, and 3 centers have begun data entry into REDCap. The projected end date of data collection is June 2027. Participating centers are encouraged to propose independent research questions leveraging the pooled dataset. As of October 2026, 23 project titles have been submitted by investigators. These proposals will be evaluated once sufficient data have been accrued. Preliminary pooled analyses are anticipated for release in July 2027. The PFO-COPA (Patent Foramen Ovale Closure Outcomes in Patients of Advanced Age) study will generate the most comprehensive real-world evidence to date on PFO closure in adults aged ≥60 years. By evaluating both effectiveness and safety in this understudied age group, the study will fill a major evidence gap and help guide clinical decision-making. Ultimately, these findings may inform future guideline updates and lay the groundwork for prospective multicenter trials focused specifically on older adults.

title: Glutamatergic Systems in Cnidaria: Glutamate Immunostaining in Hydrozoan Medusae.
abstract: The origins and early diversification of intercellular signaling molecules in animals remain poorly understood because comparative data across basal metazoan lineages are limited. Cnidarians form the sister group to bilaterian animals, and characterizing their transmitter systems is critical to understanding how complex adaptations within integrative systems shape evolutionary trajectories. Although glutamate is a well-established transmitter in bilaterian animals, its role in cnidarians remains unclear, and information on its neuronal function and signaling is limited. For most studied cnidarians, glutamate has been suggested to be a non-neuronal signaling molecule. Here, using glutamate immunoreactivity (Glu IR) in eight hydrozoan species with distinct ecologies (Aequorea victoria, Eutonina indicans, Clytia gregaria, Bougainvillia principis, Euphysa flammea, Polyorchis penicillatus, Aglantha digitalis, Nanomia septata), we identified and visualized distinct populations of glutamate-immunoreactive (Glu-ir) cells, including nematocytes, neurons, and muscle cells. A broad diversity of Glu-ir nematocytes was found in all studied species. Glu-ir neural cells were found only in three species (Aequorea, Nanomia, and Aglantha); their morphology and localization were species-specific. In addition, some striated and smooth muscle cells were found to be either Glu-ir or GABA-ir. We propose that both glutamatergic and GABAergic systems were independently recruited more than three times as neurotransmitters across cnidarians, and that these recruitments are fundamentally rooted in bioenergetic demands.
